Preserve other characters so provider IDs are not rewritten accidentally. Return `null` for `null`, `undefined`, or an all-whitespace input, and keep the function free of I/O. Acceptance: ` acme-uk_01 ` becomes `ACMEUK01`, while slash and period characters remain intact.

Update the PHP Laravel `WireTransferRequest` validation rules for domestic wires. Require `routing_number` to be exactly nine numeric digits and `account_number` to contain 4–17 digits; keep both fields strings so leading zeroes survive. Apply the existing `required_if:transfer_type,domestic` condition and leave international-wire rules untouched. Use Laravel’s standard rule syntax, not a controller-side check. Acceptance: valid zero-prefixed values pass, wrong lengths and non-digits fail, and fields are optional for international transfers.

Implement the missing Scala `FxRateService.cachedRate` method. Cache successful rates by uppercase `base/quote` pair for 60 seconds using the module’s existing in-memory cache, and call the provider only on a miss or expired entry. Do not cache provider exceptions or zero or negative rates. Preserve the existing `Future[BigDecimal]` return type and avoid blocking. Acceptance: repeated lookups within the TTL make one provider call, pair casing shares a key, expiration refreshes, and failures remain retryable.

Add the Rust `settlement_totals` function in the reconciliation module. Given completed settlement rows, sum gross, fees, and net separately by ISO currency using integer minor units; exclude rows marked reversed and preserve negative adjustments. Return a deterministically sorted `BTreeMap` keyed by currency code, without floating-point arithmetic or mutation of input rows. Acceptance includes multiple currencies, an excluded reversal, and a negative fee adjustment, with net equal to gross minus fees for every currency.

Fix the countdown in src/components/QuizTimer.tsx. It currently subtracts elapsed milliseconds twice after a browser visibility change, causing timed quizzes to expire early. Keep the existing React and TypeScript props, server-provided duration, pause semantics, and submission flow. Recompute remaining time from the original deadline, clamp it at zero, and invoke onExpire once. Acceptance: no early expiry, no negative display, exactly one callback, and the current Jest and React Testing Library suite still passes.

Fix the CSV roster importer in backend/roster/importer.py. Re-uploading the same district file currently creates duplicate Student rows when the external student ID already exists. Preserve the existing Django transaction, validation errors, and handling of genuinely new students; do not deduplicate by name or email. Make the lookup and insert path idempotent for a matching district_id plus external_id. Acceptance: repeated imports create one row, changed names update only as currently intended, and unrelated districts remain isolated.

Fix the autosave crash in app/services/lesson_draft.ts. When a teacher opens a lesson with no saved draft, the Vue and TypeScript editor dereferences undefined metadata while handling the first keystroke. Keep the current debounce interval, API payload shape, and dirty-state behavior. Normalize the missing draft to the existing empty-draft model before serializing, without changing how real drafts are merged. Acceptance: no exception, one valid autosave request, and existing draft edits behave unchanged.

Fix gradebook score rounding in lib/gradebook/score.py. The Python service rounds each rubric item before summing, so a final percentage can differ from the mathematically correct total by a point. Preserve the public function signature, Decimal-based storage, late-work penalties, and displayed two-decimal formatting. Sum unrounded weighted values first, then round only the final percentage using the repository’s existing half-up rule. Acceptance: the reported total matches the exact weighted calculation and current callers need no changes.

Fix the attendance date conversion in app/helpers/attendance_dates.rb. The Rails helper uses the server timezone when converting a teacher’s local date to the API timestamp, so evening classes near midnight are recorded on the wrong day. Use the school timezone already present on the attendance record, preserve the existing ISO-8601 output and nil behavior, and change no database schema or controller code. Acceptance: the local calendar date is retained for America/New_York around UTC midnight and all existing date cases remain green.

Fix the flashcard review reset in ios/ReviewSession.swift. After the final card, tapping Again starts a new session with the previous card index instead of the first due card, which skips material for students. Keep the current SwiftUI navigation, spaced-repetition scheduling, and persistence calls. Reset only the in-memory queue cursor when constructing the next session; do not alter card intervals or ordering rules. Acceptance: the next session begins at its first due card and existing review behavior is unchanged.

Fix homework attachment downloads in server/storage/signed_url.ts. Files with spaces or non-ASCII names currently receive malformed S3 signed URLs because the object key is encoded twice. Keep the existing AWS SDK version, bucket permissions, expiration, and response shape. Encode the raw object key exactly once at the signing boundary, while preserving the original display filename for Content-Disposition. Acceptance: the generated URL fetches the intended object and ordinary filenames remain compatible.

Fix the enrollment search query in app/Models/Enrollment.php. The Laravel scope currently applies the student-name filter with an OR that escapes the selected school, so administrators see matching students from other schools. Keep pagination, authorization checks, case-insensitive search, and the existing archived-enrollment behavior. Group the name predicates under the school constraint without changing the public scope signature. Acceptance: results never cross school boundaries, matching names remain searchable, and unfiltered results are unchanged.

Fix the parent digest grouping in src/Digest/Builder.cs. The .NET job drops a student’s unread assignment notification when two notifications share the same assignment ID, because the grouping key omits the parent recipient. Preserve delivery timing, unread filtering, localization, and the existing email template. Include parent ID in the in-memory grouping key only; do not change database queries or schema. Acceptance: each parent receives their own notification exactly once, with no duplicate emails.

Fix progress percentage caching in frontend/stores/courseProgress.ts. The Vue and TypeScript store keeps the first module total forever, so adding or removing a lesson leaves a student’s displayed completion percentage stuck. Preserve the API response contract, optimistic completion updates, and local-storage key. Invalidate or recompute the derived percentage when the module list changes, without introducing a polling loop. Acceptance: the percentage reflects the current modules, unchanged data does not trigger extra requests, and existing completion behavior remains intact.

Fix rubric total calculation in grading/rubric_total.rb. The Ruby service treats an unselected criterion as zero points but still divides by that criterion’s maximum, lowering scores for partially completed submissions. Keep the existing criterion ordering, score validation, and nil handling. Calculate the denominator from criteria that have an assigned score, while retaining the current zero result when none are scored. Acceptance: partial submissions use the scored maximum, fully scored totals remain identical, and invalid score behavior is unchanged.

Fix course archiving in api/handlers/archive_course.go. The Go handler returns a 500 when a course has no active enrollments because it dereferences an empty query result while building the audit event. Preserve authorization, transaction boundaries, audit fields, and the existing JSON response. Treat an empty enrollment list as a valid archive with a zero affected-student count, and leave the not-found course error unchanged. Acceptance: empty courses archive successfully, populated courses retain current behavior, and no schema change is needed.

Build a production multi-model inference platform in Python and Go around Kubernetes and NVIDIA Triton. It must register versioned models, schedule GPU and CPU workloads across regions, support dynamic batching, autoscaling, streaming and synchronous APIs, tenant quotas, canary rollouts, and rollback. Persist metadata in PostgreSQL and artifacts in S3-compatible storage; expose OpenTelemetry metrics, traces, and audit logs. Provide Terraform, Helm, load tests, failure recovery, and documented security boundaries. Acceptance: deploys to a fresh cluster, passes contract and stress tests, meets defined p95 latency SLOs, and demonstrates zero-downtime model rollout.

Create an end-to-end ML data flywheel for a Python and TypeScript product: capture prediction events, redact PII, deduplicate and version datasets in S3 and Delta Lake, route uncertain samples for human labeling, and feed approved labels back into training. Use Kafka, Spark, PostgreSQL, and a React review console with RBAC and immutable audit history. Support schema evolution, lineage, replay, backfills, and tenant isolation at billion-event scale. Acceptance: reproducible dataset snapshots, at-least-once processing with idempotent consumers, privacy deletion propagation, operational dashboards, disaster recovery, and integration tests covering capture through retraining.

Implement a distributed semantic retrieval platform in Rust and Python using Kafka, object storage, and a sharded vector database such as Milvus or custom HNSW and IVF indexes. It must ingest mutable documents, chunk and embed them with configurable models, support hybrid lexical and vector search, metadata filters, tenant isolation, online reindexing, snapshots, and cross-region replication. Add query tracing, relevance metrics, backpressure, and cost controls. Acceptance: versioned APIs, deterministic rebuilds, zero-downtime index upgrades, measured recall and latency benchmarks, failover recovery, and load tests at the specified corpus and QPS targets.

Build an enterprise prompt and agent orchestration platform in TypeScript and Python. Provide versioned prompt templates, model and provider adapters, structured tool calling, streaming, retries, budgets, secrets isolation, policy checks, conversation state, and asynchronous workflows with durable execution. Store metadata in PostgreSQL, events in Kafka, and artifacts in S3; expose a React console for editing, approvals, traces, and replay. Support OpenAI-compatible and local models without vendor lock-in. Acceptance: reproducible runs, idempotent retries, tenant RBAC, auditability, golden-test regression gates, rate-limit handling, and documented disaster recovery.

Develop a research-grade distributed reinforcement-learning framework in Python, JAX, and Ray for offline and online training. Implement replay storage, prioritized sampling, environment workers, learner and actor separation, checkpointing, deterministic seeding, mixed precision, experiment tracking, and pluggable PPO, SAC, and offline-dataset algorithms. Run on Kubernetes with GPU scheduling and object-store checkpoints; tolerate worker loss and resume jobs. Acceptance: reproduce published baseline scores within stated variance, scale across multiple nodes, provide profiling and cost metrics, pass numerical and integration tests, and include configuration examples plus end-to-end benchmark reports.

Replace the existing ad hoc feature pipelines with a governed online and offline feature store using Python, Scala, Kafka, Spark, PostgreSQL, and Redis or RocksDB. Define feature schemas and ownership, compute point-in-time-correct training data, serve low-latency online features, support backfills, TTLs, freshness monitoring, lineage, and safe schema evolution. Preserve historical reproducibility and isolate tenants. Acceptance: dual-read migration tooling, no training or serving skew in validation, documented SLAs, replayable pipelines, disaster recovery, access controls, and benchmark evidence for target throughput, p99 latency, and recovery time.

Build a multi-tenant GPU scheduling and quota platform for Kubernetes in Go, extending the scheduler with MIG awareness, topology and NUMA placement, gang scheduling, preemption, queue fairness, reservations, and elastic training jobs. Integrate node health, power and temperature telemetry, admission policy, and chargeback reporting; expose APIs and a React operations dashboard. It must survive control-plane and node failures and avoid orphaned allocations. Acceptance: conformance tests on supported GPU types, starvation and fragmentation benchmarks, safe upgrade and rollback, authenticated audit logs, chaos tests, and documented capacity-planning and incident-runbook procedures.

Create a continuous LLM evaluation platform in Python and TypeScript that runs curated benchmarks, adversarial safety suites, human preference studies, and production replay datasets against multiple providers and local models. Support dataset and rubric versioning, deterministic seeds, tool-use traces, judge-model calibration, statistical confidence intervals, redaction, and approval gates in CI/CD. Persist raw artifacts and lineage, with a React results explorer and API and webhook integrations. Acceptance: reproducible reports, pluggable metrics, cost and latency accounting, regression thresholds, flaky-test quarantine, access control, and scheduled distributed execution with resumable jobs.

Migrate the legacy recommendation stack from batch TF-IDF features to a distributed neural retrieval and ranking system using Python, PyTorch, Kafka, Spark, and Kubernetes. Train and version dual-encoder embeddings plus a reranker, build incremental indexes, serve online candidates, and preserve explainability and fallback behavior. Backfill historical data without interrupting traffic, support A/B and shadow launches, and meet privacy deletion requirements. Acceptance: offline relevance gains against the current baseline, online latency and availability SLOs, parity checks, rollback, reproducible training, monitoring for drift and bias, and a staged production migration plan.

Implement a cross-silo federated learning platform in Python and Rust for hospitals or edge sites, using gRPC, Kubernetes, object storage, and secure aggregation. Coordinate heterogeneous clients, retries, partial participation, differential privacy, encrypted updates, model versioning, and per-site audit logs without moving raw data centrally. Support FedAvg and at least one robust aggregation method, simulator-based testing, and offline evaluation. Acceptance: verified privacy budget accounting, resilience to malicious or unavailable clients, reproducible multi-round experiments, measurable communication reduction, compliance-oriented threat documentation, and end-to-end deployment automation for coordinator and clients.

Build a privacy-preserving synthetic tabular and time-series data service in Python using PyTorch, Spark, and Kubernetes. It must ingest governed schemas, detect sensitive columns, train configurable generative models, enforce privacy budgets, produce quality and disclosure-risk reports, and publish versioned datasets to a catalog. Include tenant isolation, approval workflows, lineage, reproducible seeds, GPU job orchestration, and deletion propagation. Acceptance: utility benchmarks against real holdouts, membership-inference and memorization tests, differential-privacy accounting, resumable distributed training, cost and latency dashboards, API and CLI clients, and documented limits explaining when generated data is unsafe for model training.

Design and implement a durable long-term memory platform for autonomous coding agents in TypeScript, Python, and PostgreSQL. Ingest conversations, tool traces, repository changes, and user preferences; extract entities and summaries, index hybrid semantic and lexical memories, enforce temporal validity and access control, and expose retrieval, write, compaction, and deletion APIs. Support multi-agent namespaces, conflict resolution, provenance, encryption, and configurable retention. Acceptance: replayable ingestion, relevance and contamination benchmarks, bounded latency at scale, tenant-isolated authorization tests, GDPR-style erasure, crash recovery, observability, and a migration path from the current ephemeral context store.

In the TypeScript Next.js storefront and Node/Prisma checkout API, fix cart totals becoming stale when a shopper changes quantity after applying a percentage or fixed-amount coupon. Recalculate discounts from the current line items on every cart mutation, keep monetary arithmetic in integer cents, and make the API authoritative for the displayed total. Preserve existing coupon eligibility rules. Add regression tests for quantity increases, removals, and fixed discounts; acceptance is matching UI/API totals and no negative subtotal.

In the React/TypeScript storefront and Express checkout service backed by PostgreSQL, fix refreshes or repeated clicks creating two orders for one checkout. Generate and persist an idempotency key per checkout attempt, enforce a unique constraint at the order boundary, and return the original order for retries. Keep the existing payment flow and user-visible confirmation intact. Add tests for double-clicks, browser refreshes, and concurrent requests; acceptance is at most one paid order and one inventory decrement per checkout.

In the Django/Python checkout service using PostgreSQL, fix concurrent purchases allowing stock to fall below zero or two buyers to receive the last unit. Perform the availability check and decrement inside one transaction with row-level locking, preserve existing reservation expiry behavior, and return the current out-of-stock response when the lock-protected quantity is insufficient. Add a concurrency test plus normal single-item coverage; acceptance is never-negative inventory and exactly one successful purchase for one remaining unit.

In the Ruby on Rails commerce app with Redis-backed guest carts, fix login merging so a guest cart is not silently overwritten by the shopper’s existing account cart. Merge matching SKUs using the existing quantity limits, retain distinct items from both carts, and clear the guest token only after a successful database update. Preserve current abandoned-cart behavior. Add request and model tests for empty, overlapping, and conflicting carts; acceptance is one correct cart after login with no duplicate lines or lost items.

In the Vue 3/TypeScript storefront and Laravel/PHP tax endpoint, fix tax disappearing after a shopper edits the shipping address or changes the postal code. Keep the prior tax estimate visible while recalculation is pending, request tax only for a valid address, and replace it with the authoritative server result rather than resetting to zero on validation or network errors. Preserve existing exemptions and currency formatting. Add component and endpoint tests; acceptance is stable totals through address edits and an explicit error state when tax cannot be calculated.

In the Java Spring Boot order service integrated with Stripe webhooks, fix orders being marked paid or released to fulfillment before a payment failure is processed. Make payment state transitions idempotent and allow only a verified success event to move an order from pending to paid; failed, canceled, and disputed events must stop fulfillment without overwriting a later valid success. Preserve existing retry handling. Add webhook fixtures and service tests for duplicate and out-of-order events; acceptance is no fulfillment for failed payments and consistent final status after replay.

In the Python FastAPI catalog service with Redis caching, fix product detail pages showing an old price after an administrator updates the product. Invalidate or version the product cache in the same successful update path, including variant prices, without disabling caching globally. Ensure cart and checkout continue to read the authoritative catalog price and retain existing cache TTLs for unrelated products. Add API and cache tests for base and variant price edits; acceptance is the new price visible immediately after update and no stale value reused across requests.

In the Next.js/TypeScript checkout and Python shipping service, fix checkout returning a 500 when a shopper enters a valid PO box address. Detect the address type before requesting carrier rates, suppress methods that do not support PO boxes, and return the existing pickup or postal option when available. Keep residential-address behavior unchanged and show a clear no-methods message when none qualify. Add API and UI regression tests; acceptance is no crash, correct eligible options, and a recoverable error state.

In the Kotlin Spring Boot order service, fix out-of-order payment and fulfillment webhooks allowing an older event to move an order backward from shipped or paid to pending. Record the provider event ID and a monotonic event timestamp or sequence, ignore duplicates, and reject transitions that violate the existing order state machine. Do not change valid cancellation behavior. Add unit tests for retries, reordered delivery, and normal progression; acceptance is a stable final status regardless of webhook arrival order.

In the SvelteKit/TypeScript product page, fix the recommendation widget showing unavailable variants as purchasable after inventory changes. Filter variants using the same availability data as the add-to-cart path, refresh that data when the widget loads, and remove only unavailable choices without hiding an otherwise available product. Preserve selected options when still valid and show the existing sold-out treatment otherwise. Add component tests for mixed inventory and an all-unavailable response; acceptance is no disabled-stock variant can be added to cart.

In the React storefront and Symfony/PHP order API, fix split-shipment summaries charging the customer’s shipping fee once per package instead of applying the existing combined-order rule. Calculate shipping from the shipment group totals, preserve free-shipping thresholds and promotion exclusions, and return one authoritative amount for both checkout and the confirmation page. Do not change carrier rate selection. Add API and UI regression tests for one, two, and mixed-rate shipments; acceptance is matching totals with no duplicate shipping charge.

In the C# ASP.NET Core refund service integrated with Stripe, fix refunds differing by a cent from the original order when discounts are allocated across multiple line items. Perform all calculations in integer cents, distribute any rounding remainder deterministically, and ensure the sum of line refunds never exceeds the captured amount. Preserve partial-refund and already-refunded checks. Add tests for odd totals, percentage discounts, and repeated partial refunds; acceptance is exact cent-level reconciliation with Stripe and the order ledger.

In the Dart/Flutter mobile analytics repository, run `mv events.csv sessions.csv` at the repository root. Do not alter contents or references. Acceptance: sessions.csv exists with identical bytes, and events.csv is absent.

In the Swift mobile analytics repo, run `awk 'NR > 1 { count++ } END { print count }' users.csv` and report the integer. Exclude the header, do not modify users.csv, and accept only the record count as output.

In the Kotlin mobile app, inspect api_samples.json for the GET /health fixture and confirm whether its status field is exactly 204. Do not edit the fixture. Acceptance: answer yes/no and quote the numeric status.
In the Flutter mobile repo, append one LF byte to metrics.json, without reformatting or changing any other bytes. Acceptance: file size increases by one byte and parsed JSON content is unchanged.

In the Flutter mobile analytics repo, group sales.csv by its date column and sum amount into daily_totals.csv with header date,total. Preserve ISO date text and leave sales.csv unchanged. Acceptance: one row per date and totals equal the direct group-by sum.

In the React Native mobile app, inspect sessions.csv and count blank or null cells separately per column, treating empty strings as missing. Do not edit the file. Acceptance: return every header with its integer missing count.

In the Swift mobile app, update AnalyticsParser.swift so timestamps read from events.csv are parsed in UTC, not device local time. Change no other fields or logic. Acceptance: timezone is explicitly UTC and existing event values are otherwise unchanged.

In the Kotlin mobile repo, remove only fully identical duplicate data rows from imports.csv, retaining the first occurrence, header, and original order. Do not deduplicate by selected columns. Acceptance: no duplicate rows remain and unique rows are byte-for-byte unchanged.

In the Flutter mobile analytics module, read summary.json and compare total_events with the sum of all per-day events values. Do not edit the file. Acceptance: return pass/fail plus both numeric totals.

In the React Native mobile repo, calculate the median of nonblank timings.csv latency_ms values, ignoring blanks only. Do not modify the source. Acceptance: return one number in milliseconds, averaging the two middle values when the count is even.

In the Swift mobile app's data folder, inspect profile_export.csv and return only its header names in original left-to-right order. Do not transform rows. Acceptance: spelling, case, punctuation, and order exactly match the CSV header.

In the Flutter mobile repo, edit chart_config.json by changing only sample_size to numeric 10. Preserve formatting and all other keys. Acceptance: valid JSON remains, sample_size equals 10, and no unrelated value changes.

Fix the React Native/TypeScript offline-sync bug where edits made on two devices can overwrite each other or vanish after reconnect. Audit the SQLite cache, background queue, API conflict handling, retry and backoff logic, and logout/account-switch cleanup on iOS and Android. Preserve server timestamps and implement deterministic conflict resolution for notes and attachments. Add migration-safe schema changes, telemetry for rejected operations, unit and integration tests, and an airplane-mode end-to-end test. Acceptance: queued edits survive restarts, conflicts follow documented policy, and no data loss occurs.

Fix deep-link handling in the React Native mobile app when a user opens an invite, password-reset, or shared-content link while logged out, refreshing a token, or already inside another modal. Coordinate Android App Links, iOS Universal Links, navigation state, pending-link persistence, and expired-token recovery without creating duplicate screens. Preserve attribution parameters and prevent untrusted URLs from reaching privileged routes. Add tests for cold start, warm start, terminated-app launch, reinstall, and account switching. Acceptance: every supported link reaches the correct destination exactly once or shows a recoverable error.

pair.short: Push alerts open the wrong place
pair.full: Fix notification routing in the Flutter/Dart app, where Firebase Cloud Messaging and APNs payloads sometimes open stale conversations, duplicate navigation stacks, or show content for the wrong account. Normalize payload parsing across iOS and Android, validate tenant and user identifiers, persist unopened notifications, and reconcile delivery with the server read state. Handle foreground, background, terminated, and notification-tap flows, including invalid or expired targets. Add mocked provider tests and device-level scenarios. Acceptance: one tap opens the intended screen, duplicate taps are idempotent, and invalid payloads never expose another user’s data.

Fix the native mobile upload subsystem where large photos and videos stop after suspension, retry from byte zero, or remain marked pending forever. The app uses Swift on iOS, Kotlin on Android, and a resumable multipart API. Rework foreground/background session handling, WorkManager and URLSession scheduling, network constraints, cancellation, disk cleanup, checksum validation, and server-side idempotency. Preserve upload progress across process death and account changes while preventing duplicate media. Add fault-injection tests for airplane mode, low storage, token expiry, and app termination. Acceptance: interrupted uploads resume safely and eventually reach one consistent server record.

Fix the Flutter checkout flow on devices with gesture navigation, hardware keyboards, dynamic type, and different IMEs. Focus currently causes fields to hide behind the keyboard, jumps the scroll position, loses validation errors, and occasionally submits twice. Replace ad hoc inset calculations with a shared form layout that handles iOS keyboard notifications, Android edge-to-edge insets, autofill, focus traversal, and nested scrolling. Keep existing analytics and payment SDK behavior. Add golden, widget, and physical-device tests. Acceptance: every field remains reachable, focus is stable during validation, and one deliberate tap produces at most one order.

Fix subscription restoration in the React Native app using StoreKit 2, Google Play Billing, and a server-side entitlement service. Restore can spin indefinitely, reattach a purchase to the previous account, or show premium access before receipt verification completes. Design one state machine for purchase, restore, pending, revoked, grace-period, and offline states; make server reconciliation idempotent; and handle store callbacks after process death. Preserve existing promotional offers and analytics. Add sandbox tests, mocked billing tests, and account-switch coverage. Acceptance: restore resolves visibly within a bounded timeout, entitlements match the authenticated account, and retries never create duplicate grants.

Fix accessibility navigation in the native SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose mobile app. VoiceOver and TalkBack currently skip dynamically inserted content, announce decorative controls, lose focus after navigation, and read validation errors out of order. Establish shared accessibility semantics for headings, grouped controls, loading states, modal dismissal, and error summaries without changing visual designs. Account for localization and dynamic type, and avoid exposing sensitive account data through announcements. Add UI automation tests using iOS VoiceOver and Android accessibility assertions. Acceptance: keyboard-equivalent flows are fully operable, focus lands predictably after updates, and critical errors are announced once.

Fix internationalization regressions in the Kotlin Multiplatform mobile app when users change locale or enable an RTL language. Dates, currencies, plurals, text expansion, cached translations, and navigation labels can disagree between screens, while some layouts remain left-to-right. Centralize locale state, formatting, resource loading, and persistence; audit Compose and SwiftUI bridges; and preserve server-controlled language preferences across login. Add screenshot and unit coverage for Arabic, German, Japanese, and French, including cold start and mid-session changes. Acceptance: no clipping or mixed locale remains, RTL mirrors correctly, and formatted values follow platform conventions.

Fix background location tracking in the native iOS and Android field-service app, where frequent GPS polling drains batteries, misses geofences, and continues after logout. Rework lifecycle ownership, permission upgrades, significant-change and fused-location strategies, batching, accuracy thresholds, and server upload scheduling. Respect platform background limits, approximate-location choices, privacy disclosures, and tenant-specific tracking policies. Add instrumentation for sampling rate and battery impact, plus simulated-route tests for killed, suspended, offline, and permission-denied states. Acceptance: trips remain accurate enough for dispatch, tracking stops promptly when required, and measured idle battery use meets the agreed budget.

Fix the Room and SQLite migration path in the Android/Kotlin app after upgrading from schema versions 12 through 16. Some users lose drafts or crash on startup because migrations assume complete rows, run twice, or leave indexes inconsistent after an interrupted upgrade. Define a forward-only migration strategy, backfill nullable fields safely, preserve encrypted records, and provide a recoverable backup and rollback boundary without silently deleting user data. Test every supported version jump, low-storage interruption, process death, and downgrade refusal. Acceptance: existing drafts and sync metadata survive all upgrades, startup never loops, and failures produce actionable diagnostics.

Fix biometric authentication in the React Native app across iOS Keychain and Android Keystore. After a failed scan, token refresh, device lockout, or logout, users can get trapped in a prompt loop or regain access under the wrong account. Redesign the credential state machine around app lifecycle events, passcode fallback, biometric enrollment changes, refresh-token rotation, secure key invalidation, and explicit cancellation. Keep security policy and analytics intact, and never log secrets. Add simulator and physical-device tests for enrollment changes, backgrounding, reinstall, multiple accounts, and offline startup. Acceptance: each failure reaches a clear recovery path and no stale credential authorizes access.

Fix the mobile checkout state bug in the React Native commerce app using Stripe PaymentSheet and a Node.js order API. After 3DS authentication, app backgrounding, webhook delay, or a network retry, the app can show paid when the order failed, create duplicate orders, or lose the confirmation screen. Define a server-authoritative order state machine, idempotency keys, webhook reconciliation, deep-link return handling, timeout recovery, and safe retry semantics. Preserve existing tax and inventory rules. Add contract, integration, and device tests. Acceptance: every payment ends in one auditable order state, retries are idempotent, and users receive accurate recovery guidance.

Fix the deadlocks in our Go CLI's remote execution coordinator, which uses gRPC workers, Kubernetes Jobs, and Redis leases. Preserve the public command and wire protocols while redesigning cancellation, retry, lease renewal, and shutdown so one lost worker cannot block a run forever. Add race and fault-injection tests, bounded goroutine and memory usage, and metrics for stuck states. Acceptance: 10,000 concurrent runs complete or fail within deadlines, cancellation is idempotent, no leaked workers remain, and existing integration suites pass on Linux and macOS.

Repair intermittent log loss and reordering for remote jobs launched by the Python CLI through a gRPC gateway, Kafka stream, and S3 archive. The fix must survive worker restarts, network partitions, retries, and jobs producing more than 100 GB of output without duplicating terminal events or exhausting client memory. Maintain existing CLI flags and archive formats, add resumable sequence-numbered collection, and migrate older workers safely. Acceptance includes deterministic replay tests, exactly-once archival semantics, bounded streaming memory, and successful recovery for 10,000 concurrent jobs.

Repair the plugin compatibility failures in our Rust CLI platform after core releases. Plugins are distributed as signed binaries and Python or Node adapters, discovered through a registry, and executed in isolated subprocesses. Preserve existing plugin commands while introducing explicit capability negotiation, stable versioned schemas, migration shims, and rollback for partially upgraded installations. The implementation must work offline and on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Acceptance requires a compatibility matrix across three major CLI versions, signature and sandbox tests, reproducible packaging, and zero command regressions in the full plugin corpus.

Fix corruption in the distributed content-addressed cache used by our Go CLI and remote build workers. The cache combines local filesystem layers, an S3-compatible object store, Redis locks, and concurrent garbage collection. Preserve cache keys and existing artifacts while making writes atomic, validating checksums, handling interrupted uploads, and preventing deletion of live entries across regions. Add repair and verification commands plus failure-injection coverage. Acceptance: no corrupted artifact after 1,000 concurrent writers, safe recovery from process and network crashes, bounded lock contention, and backward-compatible reads of all supported cache generations.

Repair cross-platform path handling throughout the TypeScript CLI, its PowerShell and Bash launchers, and the remote agent protocol. Current failures involve UNC paths, drive letters, symlinks, quoting, case sensitivity, workspace mounts, and paths serialized between Windows and Linux workers. Preserve POSIX behavior and existing configuration files while centralizing normalization and validating every boundary. Acceptance requires hermetic tests on Windows, macOS, and Linux, mixed-platform integration runs, safe rejection of traversal and ambiguous paths, reproducible archive extraction, and no regressions in commands that mount or clean workspaces.

Fix stuck rollbacks in the Go release CLI that coordinates OCI images, Kubernetes deployments, Helm charts, and an etcd-backed release ledger. Rollback must remain safe during controller restarts, partial image publication, admission failures, and concurrent deploy commands. Preserve current release manifests and audit history, but make state transitions transactional, resumable, and idempotent with explicit operator recovery for genuinely ambiguous states. Acceptance includes model-based transition tests, chaos tests across three clusters, bounded rollback time, accurate exit codes and status output, and verified recovery without deleting healthy workloads.

Eliminate credential exposure in diagnostics emitted by our Python CLI, including verbose logs, tracebacks, crash bundles, subprocess arguments, environment snapshots, and remote execution metadata. Secrets may come from AWS, Vault, Kubernetes, SSH, and plugin-provided providers. Implement centralized structured redaction with streaming-safe handling, preserve useful context, and maintain backward-compatible diagnostic schemas. Acceptance requires property-based tests against nested and encoded secrets, review of every logging path, encrypted and access-controlled crash bundles, redaction latency benchmarks, and proof that credentials never appear in local files, telemetry, or CI artifacts.

Fix destructive workspace cleanup in the Rust CLI and its distributed workspace service. Cleanup currently misidentifies shared mounts, reused persistent volumes, interrupted jobs, and workspaces with active leases, occasionally deleting user data. Preserve the existing workspace layout and command interface while adding ownership identities, lease fencing, quarantine-before-delete behavior, crash recovery, and an auditable dry-run mode. Acceptance requires filesystem and Kubernetes integration tests, simulated clock and crash tests, protection against symlink and traversal attacks, safe operation across multiple controllers, and zero deletion of active or externally owned data.

Repair telemetry overload caused by the Node.js CLI's high-cardinality events and retry storms against the central controller. The system uses OpenTelemetry, protobuf over gRPC, Prometheus, and a ClickHouse pipeline shared by thousands of agents. Preserve diagnostic coverage and existing dashboards while adding event schemas, cardinality budgets, adaptive sampling, backpressure, batching, and offline spooling. Acceptance requires load tests at 50,000 agents, bounded CPU, memory, disk, and network usage, no controller outage when telemetry is unavailable, loss accounting for sampled events, and compatibility with existing collectors and retention policies.

Fix startup races in the JavaScript CLI's profile and credential resolution system, which merges global config, project files, environment variables, cloud identity, plugins, and remote policy. Concurrent invocations can observe partially written files, stale tokens, or inconsistent precedence, especially during first-run initialization and SSO refresh. Preserve documented precedence and all existing profile formats while introducing atomic writes, process locking, transactional migrations, and deterministic resolution traces. Acceptance requires stress and crash tests across local and network filesystems, multi-process correctness, offline behavior, safe token permissions, and unchanged results for valid legacy configurations.

Fix shell completion timeouts in the Rust CLI, whose command tree is generated from plugins, remote capabilities, Kubernetes schemas, and project configuration. Completion must remain responsive when the network is unavailable, plugins are slow, or the repository contains thousands of resources. Preserve Bash, Zsh, Fish, and PowerShell output formats while introducing cached snapshots, cancellation, bounded discovery, invalidation rules, and a diagnostic mode. Acceptance requires sub-100 ms local completion, a strict two-second remote ceiling, deterministic output, no background process leaks, compatibility tests for all supported shells, and correct behavior during upgrades.

Repair state corruption in the Python CLI's multi-version migration commands for projects stored in SQLite locally and PostgreSQL remotely. Failures occur during interrupted upgrades, concurrent invocations, schema drift, partial network transactions, and downgrades from newer clients. Preserve user data and supported historical versions while adding migration journaling, preflight validation, resumable steps, backups, locking, and explicit rollback semantics. Acceptance requires upgrade and downgrade tests across ten schema generations, crash and replica-lag simulations, verification tooling, deterministic dry runs, compatibility with existing automation, and proof that an interrupted migration can resume without manual database surgery.

Refactor the Python 3.12 Click-based CLI’s `build_parser()` in `src/cli/args.py` so option registration is grouped by concern instead of repeated inline branches. Preserve every flag name, default, metavar, environment-variable fallback, and error message. Do not change command behavior or public imports. Keep the change in that file, and accept when the existing CLI test suite passes and `--help` output is byte-for-byte unchanged.

In the TypeScript Node 20 CLI, refactor `loadConfig()` in `src/config.ts` to replace its nested `if` chain with a small ordered-resolution table or equivalent readable helper. Preserve precedence: explicit `--config`, `TOOL_CONFIG`, project file, then defaults; preserve YAML parsing and current error text. Do not introduce a dependency or alter the config schema. Acceptance requires a one-file diff, passing config tests, and unchanged behavior for every precedence case.

Refactor the Go Cobra CLI’s `printVerbose()` function in `internal/output.go` to centralize repeated prefix and indentation construction. Keep normal and verbose output exactly the same, including newline placement, color-disable behavior, and stream selection. Avoid touching command wiring or adding packages. The acceptance check is a passing `go test ./...` with existing output cases still matching; the implementation should remain confined to the output file.

In `cmd/tool.py`, rename the private Python CLI helper `status_code_for_error()` to `exit_code_for_error()` and update its local references. This is a naming-only refactor: preserve integer mappings, fallback values, exception handling, and process exit behavior. Do not add a compatibility alias or new abstraction. Keep the change in this module and accept when no stale private name remains in the module and the existing CLI tests pass unchanged.

Refactor the Rust clap CLI’s `find_command()` in `src/commands.rs` to use a single local lookup map rather than repeated string comparisons. Preserve aliases, case sensitivity, unknown-command errors, and returned enum values exactly. Keep the map local to the function, avoid changing the public command API or adding crates, and retain current allocation behavior where practical. Acceptance requires the existing command-resolution tests to pass and every current alias to resolve exactly as before.

In the Ruby Thor CLI, extract the stdin/TTY check currently duplicated inside `run()` in `lib/tool/runner.rb` into one private predicate. Preserve behavior for piped input, interactive terminals, EOF, and the existing warning text. This is a readability refactor only: add no options or dependencies and change no command timing. Keep the implementation within the runner file and accept when the existing RSpec CLI tests pass.

Refactor `validate_path()` in the Bash CLI’s `scripts/tool.sh` so all path checks use one normalized variable instead of repeating `realpath` and directory tests. Preserve relative-path support, symlink handling, missing-path errors, and exact exit codes. Do not change Bash 3.2 compatibility or add external utilities. Acceptance requires the existing path-validation cases to pass and `shellcheck` to report no new issues; keep the edit confined to this script.

Refactor the JavaScript Commander CLI’s `formatHelp()` in `src/help.js` to replace manual string concatenation with the existing `padRight()` utility and a small row formatter. Preserve command ordering, spacing, ANSI color toggles, terminal-width handling, and the trailing newline. Use no new dependency and keep changes in this file. Acceptance requires the current help snapshots and `node --test` suite to pass with both color enabled and disabled.

In the Kotlin picocli CLI, extract the XDG and Windows cache-directory selection from `main()` in `src/main/kotlin/Cache.kt` into one private function. Preserve environment-variable precedence, platform-specific fallback paths, and directory-creation timing. Keep the function in the same file, do not alter public APIs or filesystem permissions, and avoid new libraries. Acceptance requires existing unit tests to pass, including cases for an XDG override and the default platform fallback.

In the PHP Symfony Console CLI, refactor `completionValues()` in `src/Completion.php` so command names and option values pass through one shared normalization path instead of separate duplicated loops. Preserve ordering, duplicate handling, quoting, and the shell-specific output format for Bash, Zsh, and Fish. Do not change the completion protocol or add packages. Keep the change to this file and accept when the existing completion fixtures and PHPStan checks pass.

Refactor the C# System.CommandLine CLI’s `WriteJsonError()` method in `src/Output/ErrorWriter.cs` to build the error payload through the existing serializer options instead of manually assembling repeated properties. Preserve JSON field names, null omission, indentation settings, stderr routing, and the nonzero exit code. Do not change the error model or add a package. Acceptance requires the current JSON-output snapshots and `dotnet test` to pass unchanged.

In the Java picocli CLI, refactor `printVersion()` in `src/main/java/com/acme/cli/VersionCommand.java` to obtain the version string through the existing metadata accessor rather than duplicating package-resource lookup logic. Preserve output text, newline behavior, fallback value, and stdout selection. Do not change command registration, manifest generation, or dependencies. Keep the edit in this file and accept when the existing version-command tests and `mvn test` pass.

In the iOS Swift project, rename the stored property `primaryColor` to `accentColor` in `Sources/Theme.swift`, updating references only within that file. Preserve its type and value. Acceptance: the file compiles and no `primaryColor` identifier remains there.

In the Android Kotlin Compose app, replace the hardcoded `8.dp` row inset with the existing `spacingSmall` dimension, which equals `8.dp`, in `app/src/main/java/ui/RowView.kt`. Preserve layout behavior. Acceptance: the file uses `spacingSmall` and the module builds.

pair.short: Remove unused UIKit import from LoginView.swift
pair.full: In the iOS SwiftUI app, remove the unused `import UIKit` line from `Sources/LoginView.swift`; retain every view declaration and import needed by the file. Acceptance: the file stays formatted, SwiftLint reports no unused-import warning, and behavior is unchanged.

In the Flutter Dart app, extract the literal `Profile` from `lib/widgets/ProfileHeader.dart` into a local `const title = 'Profile'`, then use `title` in the existing Text widget. Keep rendering identical. Acceptance: the widget compiles and displays the same title.

In the SwiftUI iOS app, inline the private `makePrimaryButton` helper into its sole call site in `Sources/SettingsView.swift`. Preserve modifiers, label text, and accessibility behavior. Acceptance: delete the helper, keep one equivalent button, and ensure the file compiles.

In the Android Kotlin Compose app, remove the inner `padding(0.dp)` modifier from `app/src/main/java/ui/HomeScreen.kt` because it has no effect. Preserve modifier order and rendered spacing. Acceptance: no zero-padding modifier remains in that chain and the module builds.

In the iOS Swift project, move the internal `formatDate(_:)` helper from `Sources/ProfileView.swift` to `Sources/DateUtils.swift`, preserving its signature and body. Update the existing call in ProfileView.swift without changing output. Acceptance: both files compile and no duplicate helper remains.

pair.short: Merge duplicate font modifiers in DetailView.swift
pair.full: In the SwiftUI iOS app, merge the two consecutive `.font(.headline)` modifiers in `Sources/DetailView.swift` into one modifier. Do not change surrounding view code. Acceptance: exactly one `.font(.headline)` remains in that chain and the view compiles.

pair.short: Split avatar URL constant in UserCell.tsx
pair.full: In the React Native TypeScript app, extract the repeated `user.avatarUrl ?? defaultAvatarUrl` expression in `src/components/UserCell.tsx` into one local `const avatarSource`. Reuse it at both image call sites. Acceptance: rendering is unchanged and `npx tsc --noEmit` passes.

In the Android Kotlin app, rename the lambda parameter `onDone` to `onComplete` throughout `app/src/main/java/checkout/CheckoutScreen.kt`, without changing its type or behavior. Acceptance: no `onDone` references remain in that file and the module compiles.

pair.short: Drop dead isLoading state in SearchView.swift
pair.full: In the iOS SwiftUI app, remove the unused `@State private var isLoading = false` declaration from `Sources/SearchView.swift` and delete no other code. Acceptance: no `isLoading` references remain, the view still compiles, and search behavior is unchanged.

In the Flutter Dart app, replace the two adjacent `SizedBox(height: 8)` widgets in `lib/screens/FeedScreen.dart` with one `SizedBox(height: 16)`. Preserve total spacing and surrounding widgets. Acceptance: the file has one equivalent spacer and `flutter analyze` passes.

Refactor the Python 3.12 asyncio bot runner so scheduling, per-task execution, and shutdown handling move out of `runner.py` into focused `scheduler.py` and `lifecycle.py` modules. Preserve the `run_bot()` API, CLI flags, concurrency limits, retry timing, and SIGTERM behavior. Update the existing pytest coverage for cancellation and graceful drain. Acceptance: the full suite passes, no task begins after shutdown is requested, every accepted task either completes or is reported failed, and Ruff plus mypy remain clean.

Refactor the Node 20 TypeScript webhook worker to centralize retry and backoff decisions in a `RetryPolicy` module instead of duplicating them across Slack, GitHub, and email handlers. Keep current exponential delays, maximum three attempts, idempotency-key behavior, and dead-letter logging unchanged. Limit changes to the worker, policy, and tests; do not alter webhook payloads or public handler signatures. Acceptance: existing Vitest tests pass, table-driven tests cover success, retryable, and permanent failures, and `npm run lint` plus `tsc --noEmit` succeed.

Refactor the Go 1.22 price-scraping bot so all site-specific timeout, user-agent, and rate-limit settings are loaded through one typed `ScraperConfig` rather than repeated constants in the Amazon, eBay, and Etsy adapters. Preserve environment-variable names, default values, request pacing, and exported adapter interfaces. Touch only configuration, adapter wiring, and focused tests. Acceptance: `go test ./...` passes, each adapter receives the expected merged config, and a missing optional variable still uses the documented default without changing crawl behavior.

Clean up the Python 3.11 agent logging path by extracting JSON formatting, correlation-ID injection, and secret redaction from the task executor into a reusable `BotLogger` helper. Preserve log levels, field names consumed by the dashboard, and existing stdout behavior; never emit tokens or webhook signatures. Update the executor tests and add redaction cases for nested dictionaries and exception text. Acceptance: pytest passes, log records remain valid JSON, every task carries its run ID, and Ruff reports no new violations.

Refactor the Rust Tokio automation worker so Redis queue polling is owned by one shared `QueuePoller` instead of each bot loop creating its own interval and connection. Preserve lease duration, visibility timeout, backpressure, and graceful cancellation semantics; keep the `Job` and `Worker` public types compatible. Split the poller into a module, update worker wiring, and add async tests with a mocked Redis client. Acceptance: `cargo test` passes, concurrent workers do not duplicate leases in the test, and shutdown closes polling without dropping already claimed jobs.

Refactor the TypeScript Temporal workflow code so workflow state transitions are represented by a single `WorkflowState` reducer rather than scattered mutations in the approval, execution, and retry activities. Keep serialized state backward-compatible with existing runs, retain timeout and retry policies, and avoid changing activity names or signal payloads. Update unit tests for every legal transition plus an unknown-event failure. Acceptance: the Temporal test environment passes, replay tests remain deterministic, and `pnpm lint` plus `pnpm typecheck` succeed.

Extract repeated Playwright browser actions from the Python 3.12 onboarding bot into a small `PortalActions` page-object module. Preserve selectors, wait conditions, screenshot-on-failure behavior, and the current login/session flow; do not introduce a new browser framework. Update the onboarding orchestration to use the module and replace duplicated mocks in its tests. Acceptance: offline pytest tests cover login, form submission, and retry after a detached page, while the existing Playwright smoke test still reaches the confirmation screen with no changes to credentials or URLs.

Normalize task payload handling in the Java 21 Spring Boot automation service by converting raw `Map<String,Object>` values at the message boundary into a validated `TaskCommand` record. Preserve JSON field names, optional-field defaults, and rejection responses for malformed jobs; downstream handlers should receive the typed record without changing business behavior. Update the Kafka listener, two handlers, and contract tests. Acceptance: Maven tests pass, old payload fixtures deserialize identically, invalid priority and missing task ID produce the current error code, and Spotless plus Checkstyle remain clean.

Replace the two nearly identical schedulers in the C# .NET 8 bot service with one `JobScheduler` that accepts a pluggable clock and dispatches both recurring and one-shot jobs. Preserve cron parsing, time-zone handling, jitter, cancellation, and metrics names, and keep dependency-injection registrations backward-compatible. Limit the refactor to scheduler code and tests. Acceptance: `dotnet test` covers daylight-saving boundaries, missed ticks, and cancellation; no job fires twice for one due time; and `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` succeeds.

Streamline notification hooks in the Elixir OTP automation service by routing Slack, email, and PagerDuty alerts through a shared `Notifier` behaviour with one normalized event struct. Preserve delivery order, retry counts, provider-specific metadata, and the existing `notify/2` call sites. Update the three adapters and ExUnit tests without changing supervision-tree topology. Acceptance: mix tests pass, a provider failure still triggers the same retry and fallback behavior, normalized events retain correlation IDs, and Credo reports no new issues.

Decouple credential loading in the Ruby 3.3 automation CLI from command implementations by introducing a `CredentialProvider` that resolves environment variables, the existing keychain, and explicit test overrides in that order. Preserve variable names, error messages, masking, and non-interactive behavior; do not add a new secrets service. Update the deploy and invite commands plus unit tests. Acceptance: RSpec verifies precedence, missing credentials fail before network calls, and command output never prints secret values; RuboCop and the existing CLI smoke test pass.

Unify automation errors in the PHP 8.3 Laravel bot backend by replacing ad hoc arrays and provider-specific exceptions with a small `AutomationError` value object and mapper at the queue boundary. Preserve HTTP status mapping, retryability, user-safe messages, and existing log context for Slack and browser jobs. Update the queue middleware, two providers, and feature tests only. Acceptance: PHPUnit covers retryable versus permanent failures, serialized failed jobs remain readable, API responses are unchanged, and PHPStan plus Laravel Pint pass.

In the existing Node.js/TypeScript payments service, add Jest tests in one test file for the `verifyStripeWebhook` helper. Cover a valid signature, a tampered payload, an expired timestamp, and malformed header input. Mock Stripe's clock or use deterministic timestamps; do not call the network or modify production code. Assert the helper returns the expected boolean or error behavior used by the current API. The test command should pass and the cases should be readable and isolated.

In the existing Python 3.12 accounting package, add one pytest module covering the `round_money` function. Test positive and negative values at exact half-cent boundaries, values already at the target precision, and zero; verify the repository's documented half-up behavior and returned `Decimal` type. Use parametrization, avoid floats where possible, and do not change implementation or global decimal context. The acceptance criterion is that the new tests pass with the current code and fail if rounding mode or sign handling regresses.

In the existing Ruby on Rails quote service, add RSpec examples for `Quote#expired?` in its existing spec file. Freeze time with the project's supported time helper and cover a quote before expiry, exactly at the expiry instant, and after expiry, including a persisted UTC timestamp. Do not introduce sleeps, database migrations, or production changes. Acceptance: deterministic specs pass in isolation and as part of the normal test command, and they clearly establish the boundary as inclusive or exclusive according to current business rules.

In the existing Go webhook handler, write table-driven tests for `RejectReplay` or the equivalent replay-window helper in one `_test.go` file. Cover a first-seen event, a duplicate event ID, an event just inside the five-minute window, and one just outside it. Use an in-memory fake store; no Redis, network, or wall-clock sleeps. Assert both the decision and store interaction count. Acceptance is `go test ./...` passing while detecting duplicate acceptance or an off-by-one window.

In the existing Kotlin/Spring payroll service, add JUnit 5 tests for `calculateWithholding` in one test class. Use `BigDecimal` fixtures for a normal paycheck, zero taxable income, and a bracket boundary; assert the configured percentage, scale, and rounding mode used by the service. Keep the tax table in test data rather than changing application configuration, and do not call Spring or external services. Acceptance: tests are deterministic, pass under the repository's Gradle test task, and fail when boundary selection or cent rounding changes.

In the existing TypeScript payment client, add Vitest coverage for `sendTransfer`'s retry behavior in one test file. Mock the HTTP adapter and use deterministic backoff or fake timers. Verify one transient 503 is retried once, a 400 is not retried, and a successful retry returns the original transfer result without issuing a duplicate idempotency key. Do not alter production code or make real requests. Acceptance: the focused test and normal suite pass, with exact call counts and error propagation asserted.

In the existing Java fraud service, add JUnit tests for `RiskBand.fromScore` in its current test file. Cover the minimum score, each documented threshold, a score immediately below and above a threshold, and the maximum valid score; also specify the behavior for an out-of-range score according to the existing contract. Use parameterized tests and no Spring context. Acceptance: the tests run with Maven, remain deterministic, and fail if a boundary uses `>` instead of `>=` or bands are reordered.

In the existing Rust import crate, add unit tests for the transaction CSV parser in one module. Cover quoted commas in merchant names, a UTF-8 currency symbol, a missing optional memo, and a malformed amount; assert the parsed cents, optional field, and error variant rather than matching unstable text. Keep fixtures inline, avoid filesystem or network dependencies, and do not change parser behavior. Acceptance: `cargo test` passes and the cases protect the current schema and validation rules.

In the existing C#/.NET ledger API, add xUnit tests for `GetTransactionsPage` in one test class. Cover the first page, a continuation token that returns the next page, an empty result, and a request larger than the maximum page size. Mock the repository and assert the item count, next token, and repository limit passed through. Make no database or HTTP calls. Acceptance: tests pass with `dotnet test` and catch token loss or incorrect limit clamping.

In the existing PHP payments library, add PHPUnit tests for `validateAchAccount` in one test file. Cover valid checking and savings inputs, an invalid routing-number checksum, unsupported account type, and missing account number. Use data providers and assert the public validation result plus the documented error code; do not contact a bank API or alter validation rules. Acceptance: the focused test and full PHPUnit suite pass, with no reliance on locale, time, or environment variables.

In the existing Swift iOS wallet module, add XCTest cases for `convert(amount:from:to:)` in one test file. Use fixed exchange-rate fixtures and `Decimal`, covering an identity conversion, a normal USD/EUR conversion, a zero amount, and a result requiring cent rounding. Assert exact currency and amount values, including the project's rounding policy. Do not fetch live rates or modify the converter. Acceptance: tests run in the existing scheme and remain stable across locale settings.

In the existing Node.js/TypeScript invoicing service, add tests for `calculateReceiptTotal` in one Jest test file. Cover line-item multiplication, a percentage discount, tax applied after discount, and a zero-item receipt; use integer cents or the project's money helper rather than binary floating-point literals. Assert the final cents and any documented breakdown fields. Do not change production code or snapshot unrelated output. Acceptance: the focused tests and normal Jest suite pass and expose tax-order or rounding regressions.

Refactor the React/TypeScript/Vite settings subsystem, which currently mixes page components, Redux slices, ad hoc fetches, and duplicated permission checks. Introduce a feature-level module structure with typed API services, shared form state, route-level loading/error boundaries, and one reusable settings navigation. Preserve existing URLs, role restrictions, autosave behavior, unsaved-change prompts, and keyboard accessibility. Migrate all account, workspace, notification, and security screens, deleting obsolete selectors and hooks. Acceptance: all existing settings flows pass, deep links and refreshes work, visual behavior is unchanged, unit and Playwright coverage is updated, and no cross-feature imports violate the new boundaries.

Refactor the React SPA shell built with TypeScript, React Router, and CSS Modules. Replace the duplicated desktop sidebar, mobile drawer, top bar, breadcrumbs, and route guards with a single layout system driven by typed navigation metadata. Preserve role- and feature-flag visibility, browser history, deep links, scroll restoration, and current responsive breakpoints while adding a clear extension point for new sections. Migrate every authenticated route and remove shell-specific state from pages. Acceptance: navigation behaves identically on supported browsers, keyboard and screen-reader flows pass, mobile drawer focus is trapped correctly, bundle size does not regress materially, and unit plus end-to-end tests cover the shared shell.

Refactor the monolithic React/TypeScript document editor into independently testable canvas, command, selection, history, toolbar, and inspector modules. Keep the existing keyboard shortcuts, undo/redo semantics, autosave protocol, collaboration cursors, and URL-based document loading. Use a single typed editor state contract and isolate rendering from mutation logic; choose stable boundaries for future plugins without introducing a new state library unless justified. Migrate all toolbar actions and side panels, remove duplicated derived state, and preserve performance for 10,000-node documents. Acceptance: existing editing behavior and persisted documents remain compatible, regression tests cover commands and shortcuts, and profiling shows no new typing or drag latency.

pair.short: Move filters out of the table
pair.full: Refactor the SPA's filtering and search architecture across the orders, users, and audit tables. Move filter parsing, serialization, validation, debouncing, and query construction out of individual React data-grid components into a shared TypeScript filter model with page-specific schemas. URLs must remain backward compatible and fully encode shareable filter state; refresh, back/forward navigation, saved views, and server pagination must continue to work. Remove duplicate local state and race-prone effects. Acceptance: all three tables use the shared primitives, invalid parameters fail safely, requests are cancelled or ignored when stale, accessibility is preserved, and unit, integration, and browser tests pass.

Refactor the application's multi-step onboarding, profile, and billing forms from custom useState/useEffect plumbing to React Hook Form with Zod schemas and shared field components. Keep the existing API payloads, server-side error mapping, conditional fields, draft persistence, file inputs, and step navigation semantics. Define a consistent validation boundary so client and server errors are distinguishable, and make every field label, description, and error accessible. Migrate all form consumers, remove legacy validators, and document schema ownership. Acceptance: valid submissions are wire-compatible, invalid and interrupted flows behave as before, keyboard navigation works, and component plus end-to-end coverage includes each conditional branch.

Refactor data access in the React/TypeScript SPA from scattered fetch calls, useEffect lifecycles, and hand-written loading flags to TanStack Query with typed API clients. Cover list, detail, mutation, pagination, and dependent-query screens without changing backend contracts. Define query keys, stale-time defaults, invalidation rules, optimistic updates, cancellation, retry policy, and a consistent error boundary strategy. Preserve permissions and offline-friendly cached reads. Migrate the dashboard, projects, activity, and admin areas, then delete obsolete hooks and duplicated caches. Acceptance: no duplicate requests occur during navigation, mutations invalidate the right views, stale responses cannot overwrite newer data, and tests verify cache behavior and failure recovery.

Refactor the SPA's visual theming from scattered hex values, component-specific overrides, and runtime class hacks into a typed design-token layer consumed by CSS variables. Support the existing light theme plus dark and high-contrast modes, system preference detection, persistence, and a safe fallback for older browsers. Migrate the shared layout, forms, tables, charts, dialogs, and marketing surfaces without changing product meaning or spacing unintentionally. Establish naming and ownership rules for color, type, spacing, radius, and elevation tokens. Acceptance: no production component contains raw theme colors, mode changes do not flash or lose state, contrast meets WCAG AA, visual regression snapshots are updated intentionally, and the bundle remains within the current budget.

Refactor all dialogs, drawers, popovers, and confirmation overlays in the React SPA into an accessible overlay manager with shared primitives and typed lifecycle events. Preserve existing deep-linkable dialogs, escape and backdrop behavior, nested confirmation flows, unsaved-form protection, and analytics events. Centralize portal mounting, z-index ordering, scroll locking, focus return, and focus trapping, while allowing route-specific content to remain separate. Migrate the settings, billing, delete, invite, and help experiences and remove one-off overlay utilities. Acceptance: screen-reader and keyboard behavior passes, nested overlays cannot leak focus, browser back closes supported overlays correctly, and visual, unit, and Playwright tests cover the migration.

Refactor notifications in the React SPA so page components no longer construct toasts, banners, inline alerts, or unread counts independently. Introduce a typed notification service and store with presentation adapters, deduplication, severity, persistence, dismissal, and telemetry rules. Keep existing server events, permission filtering, localization, and user preferences, and support both transient feedback and the persistent notification center. Migrate every producer and consumer, including mutation errors and background job updates, without changing message wording or delivery guarantees. Acceptance: notifications render consistently across routes, duplicate events collapse safely, refresh preserves required unread state, screen readers receive announcements, and tests cover ordering, retries, dismissal, and offline recovery.

Refactor authorization logic in the React/TypeScript admin and workspace UI from duplicated role checks, route guards, and conditional button code into a single typed policy model. Keep the backend authoritative: the client may hide or disable affordances but must never imply authorization is sufficient for a request. Support organization roles, resource ownership, feature flags, and permission loading failures. Migrate routes, tables, forms, menus, and bulk actions, removing stringly typed permission names and dead branches. Acceptance: existing users see the same allowed actions, unauthorized actions fail safely, policy decisions are unit-tested against a matrix of roles and resources, and end-to-end tests cover delayed or denied permission responses.

Refactor loading, error, empty, and retry handling across the React SPA into a shared state model and composable boundary components. Replace ad hoc booleans and duplicated fallback markup in dashboards, tables, forms, charts, and route loaders while preserving each screen's meaningful copy and recovery behavior. The design must distinguish initial load, background refresh, partial failure, permission denial, no results, and offline state, and it must work with TanStack Query and React Router. Acceptance: every in-scope route uses the shared primitives, transitions do not flash or erase usable data, focus moves predictably after errors, localization keys are centralized, and visual plus browser tests cover each state.

Refactor the CSV import workflow in the React/Vite SPA into explicit upload, parse, validate, preview, submit, and result stages. Move file parsing and row validation into typed services, use a Web Worker for large files, and keep UI state serializable so users can resume drafts and retry failed submissions. Preserve accepted formats, column mappings, duplicate handling, server error messages, permissions, and analytics events. Migrate the importer, mapping dialog, progress view, and history screen while removing duplicated parsing code. Acceptance: existing imports produce identical payloads, 100,000-row files keep the UI responsive, cancellations are safe, partial failures are recoverable, and unit, integration, and browser tests pass.

pair.short: Rename Open to Show Window in src/tray.ts
pair.full: In the Electron + TypeScript desktop app, edit `src/tray.ts` and change the tray menu label exactly from `Open` to `Show Window`. Do not alter the click handler or other labels. Acceptance: the tray menu shows `Show Window` and the file still type-checks.

pair.short: Bind Ctrl+Shift+P to Settings in src/menu.ts
pair.full: In the Electron + React + TypeScript desktop app, update `src/menu.ts` so the `Ctrl+Shift+P` accelerator opens the existing Settings window. Preserve all other shortcuts and menu entries. Acceptance: pressing that shortcut opens Settings once, with no new dependency or UI change.

pair.short: Set window title to Focus in src/window.ts
pair.full: In the Electron + TypeScript desktop app, set the BrowserWindow title in `src/window.ts` from `Dashboard` to `Focus`. Keep dimensions, preload configuration, and window behavior unchanged. Acceptance: the desktop window title is exactly `Focus` when launched, and TypeScript compilation remains clean.

pair.short: Change Licence to License in src/components/About.tsx
pair.full: In the Electron + React desktop app, edit `src/components/About.tsx` and replace the visible word `Licence` with `License`, preserving surrounding copy, styling, and behavior. Acceptance: the About dialog displays `License` and no other text changes.

In the Electron + TypeScript desktop app, remove only the statement `console.log('ready')` from `src/updater.ts`. Leave updater control flow, imports, and logging of other messages unchanged. Acceptance: the exact ready log is absent and the file passes lint.

pair.short: Add a newline at EOF of src/preferences.json
pair.full: In the Electron + TypeScript desktop app, add exactly one terminating newline to `src/preferences.json` without changing its JSON content or formatting. Acceptance: the file still parses as identical JSON and ends with one newline; no other files are modified.

pair.short: Update default theme to dark in src/settings.json
pair.full: In the Electron + React desktop app, edit `src/settings.json` and change only the `theme` value from `light` to `dark`. Preserve all other settings and JSON formatting. Acceptance: a fresh launch uses dark theme by default and every unrelated setting is unchanged.

In the Electron desktop app, change the `version` field in the root `package.json` from `1.4.1` to `1.4.2`. Do not edit dependencies, scripts, or lockfiles. Acceptance: package metadata reports exactly `1.4.2` and the lockfile remains untouched.

pair.short: Hide Export in compact mode in src/components/Toolbar.tsx
pair.full: In the Electron + React + TypeScript desktop app, update `src/components/Toolbar.tsx` so the existing `Export` button is hidden only when compact mode is active. Preserve export behavior in normal mode. Acceptance: compact mode renders no Export button; normal mode still renders and works.

pair.short: Remove the beta badge from src/components/About.tsx
pair.full: In the Electron + React desktop app, remove the visible `Beta` badge from `src/components/About.tsx` while leaving the About dialog layout, version text, and styling unchanged. Acceptance: the badge is absent and all other About content remains identical.

In the Electron + TypeScript desktop app, set `webPreferences.spellcheck` to `true` in the existing editor BrowserWindow definition in `src/windows/editor.ts`. Do not change other preferences. Acceptance: the editor window enables spellcheck and its current loading behavior is unchanged.

pair.short: Restore package.json macOS icon to assets/app.icns
pair.full: In the Electron desktop app, update the macOS build icon path in root `package.json` from `assets/icon.icns` to `assets/app.icns`. Do not change Windows/Linux targets or other build settings. Acceptance: macOS packaging resolves `assets/app.icns` and the JSON remains valid.

Refactor the cross-platform Electron/TypeScript desktop app into a ports-and-adapters architecture. Separate renderer, main-process, domain, persistence, and OS integrations into workspace packages; replace direct imports with typed command/query ports; preserve plugin APIs and Windows/macOS/Linux behavior. Add dependency-boundary checks, unit/contract/e2e coverage, migration shims, and architecture docs. Acceptance: existing workflows and packaging are behaviorally equivalent, CI passes on all three OSes, forbidden dependency edges fail builds, and startup time does not regress by more than 10%.

Break up the monolithic C++20/Qt6/QML desktop editor into independently testable core, document-model, indexing, synchronization, and UI-shell modules. Keep the public scripting API and file formats backward compatible, use CMake targets with explicit dependency direction, move blocking work off the GUI thread, and introduce stable interfaces for platform services. Add unit, fuzz, integration, and packaging tests. Acceptance: existing projects open and save identically, all supported OS packages build reproducibly, no module cycle remains, and benchmarked editing latency stays within 5%.

Refactor the Electron, React, and Node desktop client’s scattered JSON, SQLite, and keychain persistence into a versioned storage platform. Define a transactional repository API, encrypted-at-rest secrets handling, schema migrations with rollback, crash-safe writes, import/export, and a one-time migration for existing installations. Keep offline behavior and documented data formats compatible; never lose user data. Acceptance: migration succeeds on representative multi-year profiles, interrupted upgrades recover automatically, corruption tests pass, and all reads and writes go through the new storage service.

Refactor the C#/.NET 8 WPF desktop CAD client so the UI no longer owns domain behavior. Move business rules, geometry operations, and validation into a headless reusable library; replace view-model-to-database calls with application services and asynchronous commands; retain existing XAML workflows, add-in compatibility, and file serialization.
