Use dependency injection, nullable correctness, deterministic fixtures, and a compatibility façade during migration. Acceptance: headless tests cover core scenarios, UI smoke tests pass, add-ins continue loading, and opening and saving benchmark files match current results.

Refactor the Electron 25/TypeScript desktop IDE’s process model: remove renderer nodeIntegration, enforce contextIsolation and sandboxing, and replace ad-hoc IPC with generated, versioned RPC contracts. Move indexing, language-server orchestration, and filesystem work into supervised utility processes with cancellation, backpressure, crash recovery, and structured telemetry. Preserve extensions and existing workspace behavior across Windows/macOS/Linux. Acceptance: security review finds no direct privileged renderer access, fault-injection tests restart workers without losing edits, IPC contract tests pass, and cold-start and memory budgets stay within 10%.

Refactor the Rust/Tauri desktop analytics app’s plugin system from in-process dynamic libraries to an out-of-process capability runtime. Define a versioned manifest and permission model, isolate plugins with WASI or controlled subprocesses, stream typed messages, enforce resource limits, and provide migration support for current plugins. Keep plugin results and configuration compatible; support Windows, macOS, and Linux signing rules. Acceptance: malicious and crashing plugins cannot access unauthorized files or take down the host, old plugins have a documented migration path, deterministic integration tests pass, and packaging remains reproducible.

Refactor the Kotlin/Compose Desktop research notebook’s local synchronization layer into an offline-first, multi-device sync engine. Use a documented CRDT or equivalent conflict model, durable operation logs, resumable checkpoints, encryption, schema-version negotiation, and deterministic merge tests; keep notebooks usable without network access and preserve existing export formats. The migration must handle years of legacy journals and intermittent connectivity. Acceptance: convergence tests pass across randomized reorder, duplication, and partition scenarios, upgrades are lossless, sync resumes after crashes, and CPU, storage, and bandwidth remain within agreed budgets.

Refactor the Swift 6/AppKit desktop IDE’s legacy extension architecture into signed, sandboxed XPC services with capability-scoped APIs. Separate stable extension contracts from internal editor types, add semantic version negotiation, lifecycle supervision, permission prompts, and a compatibility bridge for existing extensions. Maintain current menus, language tooling, and settings behavior on supported macOS releases. Acceptance: extensions cannot access undeclared resources, host crashes do not terminate the editor, API conformance and upgrade tests cover every shipped extension, and notarized release builds install and recover cleanly.

Refactor the C++/Vulkan scientific visualization desktop application so rendering, data preparation, and interaction no longer block the UI. Introduce a frame scheduler, GPU-resource ownership layer, worker pipelines, cancellation, and deterministic CPU fallback while preserving camera behavior, file formats, and plug-in render passes. Support Windows and Linux drivers through the existing compatibility matrix. Acceptance: stress scenes remain interactive during loads, device loss recovers without process restart, render outputs match golden images within tolerance, and profiling shows no unbounded queue or resource leak.

Refactor the legacy Java/Swing desktop trading terminal from embedded RMI and platform-specific sockets to a versioned protobuf RPC layer shared by UI, market-data, and risk components. Provide connection lifecycle management, timeouts, retries, ordering guarantees, backpressure, and audit logging without changing trading semantics. Run old and new transports behind a compatibility adapter during rollout, and support air-gapped deployments. Acceptance: replayed sessions produce identical decisions, fault-injection tests cover disconnects and duplicates, latency and loss budgets are met, and migration can roll back per installation.

Refactor the Python/PySide6 desktop machine-learning workbench’s background execution into a durable local job platform. Separate scheduling, workers, artifact storage, and UI observation; support process isolation, GPU and CPU resource quotas, resumable checkpoints, cancellation, retries, and optional remote workers over authenticated gRPC. Preserve existing project manifests and result formats. Acceptance: queued jobs survive app restarts, failed workers do not corrupt artifacts, concurrent workloads respect quotas, old projects run unchanged, and integration tests cover crash recovery, version skew, and offline operation.

Refactor the Objective-C/Swift macOS audio workstation’s direct Core Data and filesystem access into domain, project, cache, and media-storage services. Introduce transactional project snapshots, background migration, content-addressed media, deduplication, crash recovery, and compatibility readers for existing sessions, while keeping real-time audio paths allocation-safe and deterministic. Support large projects and external drives. Acceptance: every shipped session opens and renders identically, interrupted migrations are recoverable, no UI-thread I/O remains, storage integrity checks detect corruption, and performance and regression suites meet current latency and memory budgets.

In the ESP-IDF C++ BLE client, add host-side unit tests for the reconnect state machine in `ble_client.cpp` using Unity/CMock. Cover link loss during discovery, exponential backoff capped at five attempts, successful resubscription, and cancellation when shutdown starts. Do not require a physical peripheral; inject NimBLE callbacks and use a fake clock. Acceptance: tests are deterministic, assert callback ordering and attempt count, pass under the existing `idf.py test` target, and leave production behavior unchanged.

For the FreeRTOS C firmware MQTT wrapper, write tests around broker disconnect and reconnect handling in `mqtt_transport.c` and its fake client. Use Unity with CMock, keeping tests runnable on the host without network access. Cover an outage while a QoS 1 publish is queued, retry backoff, duplicate-ack suppression, and clean recovery after reconnect. Acceptance: queued data is published once, retry timing is asserted with a controllable clock, errors are surfaced to the event callback, and the new suite passes through the repository's CMake test command.

Add unit coverage for the battery protection policy in the Zephyr C module `power_manager.c`. Use Zephyr ztest and fake ADC readings; do not exercise hardware or alter thresholds. Test low-voltage shutdown, hysteresis around the recovery threshold, charger-present behavior, and invalid ADC samples. Acceptance: each transition is asserted, the shutdown callback fires exactly once per episode, boundary values are covered, and `west test -T power_manager` passes on a clean host build.

In the ESP-IDF OTA updater, add integration-style tests for rollback decisions across `ota_manager.c`, the boot-status adapter, and the existing flash mock. Use Unity/CMock with an in-memory partition table. Cover a first-boot health-check failure, a successful confirmation before timeout, an already-invalid previous image, and a power loss between write and mark-valid. Acceptance: the selected partition and boot flags match the documented policy, no real flash or network is used, and the tests run under the existing host test target.

Write unit tests for the button debounce state machine in the Arduino/PlatformIO C++ firmware. Keep the production debounce interval unchanged and drive events through the existing fake `millis()` clock. Cover bouncing edges, a stable press, a stable release, repeated presses inside the lockout window, and wraparound of the 32-bit millisecond counter. Acceptance: exactly one logical event is emitted per transition, timestamps are deterministic, tests run without a board, and `pio test -e native` passes.

Expand the Rust Embassy provisioning test suite for Wi-Fi credentials and device certificates. Use the repository's host-side mock storage and Tokio test runtime rather than an MCU. Cover missing credentials, truncated certificate blobs, retry after a transient flash write error, idempotent reprovisioning, and zeroization of replaced secrets where observable through the API. Acceptance: errors map to the documented enum variants, storage writes are not duplicated, no network calls occur, and `cargo test -p provisioning` passes with the existing feature flags.

Add parser-focused tests for malformed telemetry frames in the MicroPython gateway's `telemetry.py`, using pytest and the existing byte-fixture helpers. Cover truncated CBOR, unknown field types, out-of-range signed readings, duplicate sequence numbers, and invalid UTF-8 device IDs. The parser must reject bad frames without raising uncaught exceptions or mutating the last valid sample. Acceptance: each rejection returns the documented error value, valid frames still parse, and `pytest tests/test_telemetry.py` passes without serial hardware.

For the STM32 HAL C++ power controller, create tests around deep-sleep entry and wake-source selection in `sleep_controller.cpp`. Use the existing mocked RTC, GPIO, and watchdog interfaces; no target board is needed. Cover timer-only wake, GPIO wake with a pending interrupt, invalid zero-duration sleep, and repeated sleep calls after a wake. Acceptance: peripherals are configured in the expected order, wake reasons are reported once, cleanup always runs, and the project's Catch2 host test target passes.

Add Go tests for the Linux gateway's I²C sensor adapter and its retry policy. Use the existing fake bus to simulate NACKs, short reads, and a bus-recovery failure; do not access `/dev/i2c-*`. Cover one successful retry, exhaustion at the configured limit, preservation of the last good reading, and conversion of permanent failures into the package error type. Acceptance: retry delays use the injected clock, no extra reads occur after failure, metrics count attempts correctly, and `go test ./...` remains green.

Write tests for authorization of remote actuator commands in the Zephyr C command router. Use ztest with a fake device identity and nonce store. Cover an allowed command with a valid capability, wrong-device signatures, expired timestamps, replayed nonces, and malformed payloads; keep cryptography mocked at the boundary. Acceptance: rejected commands never reach the GPIO driver, each rejection maps to the documented status code, nonce persistence is verified, and the focused `west test` target passes without radio hardware.

Extend the Rust embedded telemetry tests for timestamp correction in `time_sync.rs`. Use the existing deterministic clock and mock RTC, not wall-clock time. Cover positive and negative offset corrections, drift beyond the maximum slew rate, rollover near the 32-bit epoch boundary, and an update arriving while a sample is queued. Acceptance: corrected timestamps remain monotonic, slew limits are enforced, queued samples use the documented policy, and `cargo test -p telemetry --features host` passes.

Add regression tests for migrating retained device configuration from schema v1 to v2 in the ESP-IDF C++ settings layer. Use the existing NVS mock and fixture blobs; do not touch real flash. Cover a complete v1 record, missing optional fields, corrupt length metadata, already-v2 data, and an interrupted write followed by reboot. Acceptance: defaults and renamed fields match the migration spec, corrupt data is rejected safely, migration is idempotent, and the relevant `idf.py test` suite passes.

Create a multi-layer test program for the TypeScript/NestJS referral and prior-authorization subsystem. Cover controller, service, PostgreSQL repository, Redis workflow state, FHIR R4 mapping, payer rules, retries, and audit events. Use Jest, Supertest, Testcontainers, and deterministic clock/UUID helpers; do not call real payer or EHR services. Include unit, contract, integration, and failure-path cases for duplicate referrals, missing consent, partial responses, and idempotent retries. Acceptance: CI runs the suite in parallel, coverage thresholds are defined for critical packages, and all tests pass against fresh containers.

Build a comprehensive FHIR R4 validation suite for the Python/FastAPI clinical-document ingestion pipeline. Test JSON and XML bundles, profile selection, terminology bindings, required extensions, malformed resources, and cross-resource references for Patient, Observation, MedicationRequest, and Encounter. Use pytest, Hypothesis, and a pinned local validator package; fixtures must be de-identified and no network calls allowed. Add API, parser, and persistence integration tests with actionable error assertions. Acceptance: valid bundles are stored unchanged with provenance, invalid bundles return stable machine-readable errors, and the suite runs reproducibly in CI.

Implement a reusable mock and test harness for the React/TypeScript patient-search application and its GraphQL gateway. Model pagination, fuzzy matches, duplicate patients, authorization failures, rate limits, stale caches, and inconsistent demographics across MPI and EHR sources. Use MSW for browser requests, GraphQL fixtures, and Playwright for critical flows; keep PHI synthetic and isolate time and randomness. Acceptance: unit and component tests consume the same scenarios, end-to-end tests cover keyboard and accessibility behavior, and developers can add a new search scenario without editing production code.

Introduce consumer-driven contract tests between the Kotlin/Spring lab-order service, the Node.js results adapter, and external lab integration boundaries. Capture schemas and semantics for order creation, specimen status, result corrections, reference ranges, units, and cancellation events, including backwards-compatible evolution. Use Pact, WireMock, PostgreSQL Testcontainers, and versioned synthetic HL7 v2 messages; never contact live laboratories. Acceptance: contracts run in pull requests, provider verification covers every published consumer version, breaking changes fail with readable diffs, and an explicit compatibility policy documents deprecation and rollout expectations.

Build a snapshot-based regression suite for the Ruby on Rails care-plan editor and its Vue frontend. Establish canonical, de-identified scenarios for goals, interventions, recurrence, permissions, localization, timezone boundaries, and optimistic conflict resolution. Use RSpec request and component tests plus Playwright snapshots with stable fonts, seeded data, and normalized generated IDs; avoid brittle pixel-only assertions by checking semantic DOM state as well. Acceptance: snapshots are reviewed in CI artifacts, intentional updates require an explicit command, and the suite catches API/UI drift across supported care-plan versions.

Design and implement a versioned fixture library and test matrix for the Go claims adjudication service. Cover 837P and 837I intake, payer edits, coordination of benefits, reversals, duplicate detection, remittance mapping, eligibility gaps, and audit trails. Use Go test, golden files, builders, and local PostgreSQL plus object-storage emulators; all data must be synthetic and traceable to a scenario description. Acceptance: every fixture has expected adjudication outcomes and explainable rule hits, malformed claims have negative tests, and adding a new payer profile does not duplicate shared setup.

Expand automated validation tests for the Java/Spring patient-consent subsystem spanning REST APIs, database constraints, event publication, and clinician UI permissions. Exercise consent capture, withdrawal, expiration, delegated authority, minor-to-adult transition, emergency access, and revocation propagation to downstream services. Use JUnit 5, Testcontainers, WireMock, and Playwright with a fixed clock; verify audit records never expose unnecessary PHI. Acceptance: forbidden reads are blocked consistently, events are idempotent and ordered, migration tests cover existing records, and CI reports coverage for policy branches.

Create a property-based test generator and harness for the Kotlin clinical-notes service, including note sections, authorship, amendments, signatures, terminology codes, and embedded references. Generated cases must respect domain invariants while intentionally producing boundary and invalid combinations for the REST API, FHIR mapper, and Elasticsearch indexer. Use Kotest property testing, seeded runs, local containers, and synthetic data only. Acceptance: shrinking yields minimal reproducible failures, seeds are logged in CI, parser and serializer round trips preserve meaning, and the suite covers concurrent amendment conflicts without depending on production indexes.

Add property-based and model-based tests for the TypeScript scheduling subsystem used by patient and clinician calendars. Cover recurring appointments, daylight-saving transitions, time zones, holidays, provider availability, overbooking rules, cancellations, and concurrent rescheduling. Use Vitest, fast-check, and a small reference model; run database-backed scenarios with an ephemeral PostgreSQL instance and fake timers. Acceptance: generated schedules never produce overlapping confirmed visits unless policy allows it, all mutations are idempotent, counterexamples are replayable from seeds, and API, queue, and calendar-view tests agree on UTC and display-time semantics.

Build an integration-test environment for the Python/Django insurance-eligibility workflow, covering REST intake, Celery jobs, Redis state, PostgreSQL persistence, webhook callbacks, and retry/dead-letter behavior. Simulate multiple payer response formats, timeouts, ambiguous coverage, member mismatches, and same-day coordination-of-benefits changes using contract-backed stubs. Use pytest, factory_boy, Testcontainers, and a fake clock; no real payer credentials or PHI. Acceptance: the suite verifies eventual consistency and idempotency, exposes traceable job failures, runs in CI within an agreed budget, and documents which scenarios remain provider-specific.

Establish golden-file tests for the C#/.NET clinical data export service that produces CSV, NDJSON, and FHIR R4 bundles for patients, encounters, medications, and audit metadata. Include schema versions, null handling, escaping, Unicode, large records, redaction policies, and deterministic ordering. Use xUnit, Verify, seeded SQL Server containers, and synthetic fixtures; normalize timestamps only where policy permits. Acceptance: approved output changes require reviewable diffs, export manifests include counts and checksums, redacted fields never reappear in any format, and compatibility tests cover the two previous schema versions.

Create a performance and resilience test suite for the Rust/Axum clinical observations API and its PostgreSQL, Redis, and queue dependencies. Model realistic concurrent reads, writes, FHIR bundle uploads, authorization checks, bursty clinic traffic, slow downstream terminology calls, and failover. Use k6 for workload generation, Docker Compose for repeatable environments, seeded synthetic tenants, and OpenTelemetry assertions; do not use production data. Acceptance: baseline latency, throughput, error-rate, and resource budgets are documented, tests run in CI for smoke load and nightly for stress, and failures identify the saturated dependency with a reproducible report.

Build a research-grade test platform for the distributed cart and pricing services. Use TypeScript and Python with Kafka, PostgreSQL, Redis, Playwright, and k6. Add property-based and metamorphic tests for promotions, tax recalculation, abandoned-cart recovery, and concurrent updates; contract tests between services; deterministic fixture generation; and production-incident replay. Acceptance requires reproducible failures, parallel CI sharding, coverage across supported currency and catalog combinations, latency and race-condition reports, and documented local execution against containerized dependencies.

Create a comprehensive verification system for a multi-country marketplace tax engine written in Go, backed by PostgreSQL and Kafka, with external tax-provider adapters. Build golden datasets for jurisdiction, exemption, rounding, and effective-date rules; differential tests against provider sandboxes; contract tests for seller and checkout APIs; mutation testing; and replayable historical orders. Acceptance requires deterministic results across time zones, provider outages, versioned rule migrations, parallel CI execution, audit-ready reports, and documented procedures for adding jurisdictions without weakening existing coverage.

Develop a distributed resilience and test harness for the checkout platform, using Java services, Kubernetes, Temporal workflows, Kafka, PostgreSQL, and Stripe sandbox integrations. Cover retries, idempotency, payment authorization, inventory reservation, fraud holds, partial outages, duplicate webhooks, and recovery after region loss. Add deterministic fault injection, contract tests, end-to-end browser scenarios, soak tests, and trace correlation. Acceptance requires repeatable chaos experiments in CI and staging, no double charges or orders under injected failures, bounded recovery-time measurements, and actionable artifacts for every failed scenario.

Build an end-to-end test and relevance-evaluation platform for a catalog search rebuild using TypeScript ingestion services, Python evaluation jobs, Kafka, OpenSearch, and PostgreSQL. Test CDC ingestion, schema evolution, multilingual analyzers, faceting, typo tolerance, ranking changes, deleted products, and zero-downtime reindexing. Include generated catalog fixtures, labeled query benchmarks, property-based filter combinations, load tests, and differential comparison with the legacy search. Acceptance requires reproducible relevance scores, regression thresholds in CI, shard-scale performance reports, and safe validation of index migrations before production rollout.

Implement a full workflow-test platform for returns, exchanges, refunds, and warehouse disposition across event-driven services. The stack is Kotlin, Kafka, PostgreSQL, Temporal, and a third-party payments sandbox. Cover authorization policies, fraud review, partial shipments, split refunds, damaged goods, international duties, duplicate events, timeout recovery, and eventual consistency. Add consumer-driven contracts, state-machine tests, synthetic order generation, event replay, and database invariant checks. Acceptance requires exhaustive transition coverage, idempotent refund proofs, parallel CI execution, production-like staging runs, and understandable failure timelines.

Create an adversarial testing and evaluation system for the merchant fraud-detection platform. Use Python model services, Scala/Spark feature pipelines, Kafka, Redis, PostgreSQL, and a versioned feature store. Build privacy-safe synthetic identities, temporal leakage checks, replayable labeled datasets, threshold and calibration tests, fairness slices, drift simulations, and API contract tests. Acceptance requires reproducible offline and online metrics, shadow-mode comparison against the incumbent model, alerting for feature incompatibility or data leakage, explainable failure artifacts, and gated promotion of models through development, staging, and production.

Build a distributed consistency-test platform for inventory synchronization across warehouses, stores, marketplaces, and regional caches. Use Go services, Kafka, PostgreSQL, Redis, Kubernetes, and a simulated warehouse API. Add model-based tests for reservations, releases, oversells, backorders, reconciliation, replay, clock skew, network partitions, and out-of-order events; include property-based concurrent workloads and long-running soak tests. Acceptance requires measurable convergence guarantees, detection of lost or duplicated stock movements, repeatable multi-region fault scenarios, CI-scale smoke suites, and detailed divergence reports suitable for release approval.

Develop a research-grade validation harness for the online and offline recommendations stack using Python, Spark, Kafka, Feast, Redis, PostgreSQL, and Kubernetes. Test feature freshness, training-data joins, leakage, batch-to-online parity, cold-start behavior, ranking quality, diversity, latency, and fallback logic. Support deterministic dataset snapshots, replayed user sessions, statistical confidence intervals, counterfactual evaluation, and shadow traffic. Acceptance requires reproducible experiment manifests, automated data-quality gates, model-versus-baseline reports, load-test thresholds for peak traffic, and CI checks that block incompatible feature or schema changes.

Create a large regression and fuzz-testing system for the promotions rules engine, including its DSL, admin APIs, cart integration, and scheduled campaign workers. Use Java, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Kafka, and a Kubernetes test environment. Implement property-based generators for coupons, stacking, exclusions, customer segments, time windows, currencies, and catalog changes; differential tests against the legacy engine; contract tests; and concurrency and performance suites. Acceptance requires semantic-equivalence reports, mutation-score targets, deterministic shrinking of failing cases, safe rule migrations, and CI evidence for every supported promotion combination.

Build the verification program for migrating order processing from a monolithic Java/PostgreSQL application to event-driven services using Debezium, Kafka, and Go consumers. Cover dual writes, CDC ordering, backfills, schema evolution, replay, exactly-once business effects, reconciliation, cutover, rollback, and historical data correctness. Provide generated and production-sanitized fixtures, shadow comparisons, invariant checks, failure injection, and migration soak tests. Acceptance requires zero unexplained order or payment divergence, resumable test runs, quantified lag and recovery metrics, signed reconciliation reports, and automated go/no-go gates for each rollout phase.

Develop a test platform for localized pricing and scheduled price changes across regions, currencies, tax modes, channels, and customer segments. Use TypeScript and Go services with PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, and a React administration surface. Add property-based monetary calculations, exchange-rate snapshot tests, effective-date boundary cases, rounding and display tests, cache invalidation checks, authorization tests, and high-volume schedule simulations. Acceptance requires no precision or cross-region leakage defects, deterministic historical repricing, contract coverage for every channel, performance thresholds under campaign load, and audit-ready reports for releases.

Build a data-quality and reproducibility test framework for seller analytics across ingestion, transformation, and reporting layers. The stack uses Python, SQL/dbt, Spark, Kafka, and Snowflake, with dashboards consuming curated revenue, returns, attribution, and payout facts. Add schema contracts, freshness and completeness checks, reconciliation to orders and payments, late-arriving data scenarios, privacy assertions, backfill tests, statistical anomaly detection, and snapshot-based dashboard validation. Acceptance requires isolated CI datasets, lineage-linked failures, deterministic reruns, partition-scale performance reports, and certified metrics before any warehouse or model change ships.

Update the GitHub Actions CI for the TypeScript browser extension. Run pnpm install with the lockfile, lint, unit tests, and a production Vite build on pushes and pull requests; use Node 20, dependency caching, and least-privilege permissions. Keep Firefox and Chromium builds in the same workflow, fail on any command error, and upload logs only on failure. Acceptance: clean PRs pass all checks, broken tests block merging, and no generated credentials are committed.

Introduce separate dev, beta, and stable release configurations for the Manifest V3 Chrome and Firefox extension. Select the channel from a GitHub Actions workflow input, apply channel-specific manifest version suffixes and API base URLs from repository variables, and produce a uniquely named ZIP artifact for each run. Do not duplicate source files or expose secrets. Acceptance: each channel builds reproducibly, stable retains valid semver metadata, and artifacts are downloadable from the workflow run.

Configure automated signing for the existing WebExtension release workflow using GitHub Actions. Build the TypeScript/Vite package once, sign the Chrome artifact with Web Store credentials and the Firefox artifact with AMO API credentials stored only as repository secrets, and restrict signing to version tags. Ensure temporary files are cleaned up and secrets never appear in logs. Acceptance: a tag produces both signed artifacts, unsigned pull-request builds still work, and a missing credential fails with a clear error.

Add production source-map handling to the Vite build and tagged-release workflow for the browser extension. Generate maps for debugging, upload them to Sentry with the git SHA as the release identifier using SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, then exclude map files from the published Chrome and Firefox ZIPs. Keep local development unchanged and prevent tokens from entering artifacts or logs. Acceptance: Sentry resolves a release stack trace, published ZIPs contain no maps, and a failed upload stops the release.

Create a GitHub Actions pull-request workflow for the TypeScript browser extension. Install with pnpm, build both Chromium and Firefox variants through the existing Vite configuration, package each as a ZIP, and upload them as short-lived workflow artifacts without publishing to either store. Use Node 20 and a lockfile-only install. Acceptance: every PR exposes two downloadable artifacts, artifact names include the PR number and commit SHA, failed builds report clearly, and no production credentials are required.

Create a manual GitHub Actions release workflow for the existing Manifest V3 extension. Accept a version and target store input, verify the package manifest matches the requested semver, build with pnpm and Vite, then publish the selected ZIP to the Chrome Web Store or Firefox Add-ons API. Require an annotated tag or explicit confirmation, retain the uploaded artifact, and emit a concise deployment summary. Acceptance: invalid versions fail before upload, each store receives the correct package, and rerunning a release is safe.

Rotate the browser extension's CI credentials without changing runtime behavior. Replace the existing Chrome Web Store, Firefox AMO, and Sentry tokens with newly named GitHub Actions secrets, update all workflow references, remove legacy variable names and local secret examples, and document the required secret names in the repository README. Keep secrets masked and out of generated bundles. Acceptance: a release dry run succeeds with the new names, secret scanning finds no values, and old names are unused.

Add a Docker-based build environment for the TypeScript browser extension using Node 20, pnpm, and the existing Vite and web-ext tooling. Pin the package-manager version, install dependencies from the lockfile, run lint, tests, and both browser builds, and leave credentials outside the image. Update the GitHub Actions workflow to use the image or its documented command. Acceptance: `docker build` succeeds, a container run produces reproducible Chrome and Firefox artifacts, and no secrets or host-specific paths are embedded.

Add a post-build smoke-test job for the Chrome and Firefox extension artifacts using Playwright and the existing TypeScript test setup. Install each ZIP into a temporary browser profile, verify the Manifest V3 service worker starts, exercise one content-script flow, capture console errors, and publish failure traces as workflow artifacts. Run this only after packaging and before store publication. Acceptance: a broken manifest or startup error blocks release, successful runs record both browser versions, and temporary profiles are cleaned up.

Add a required GitHub Actions policy job for the Manifest V3 browser extension. Build the production bundle with pnpm and inspect the generated manifest for an approved permission and host-permission allowlist, reject unexpected debug flags, and fail when either Chrome or Firefox ZIP exceeds 5 MB. Keep the checks deterministic and expose violations in the job summary. Acceptance: branch protection can require the job, a newly added permission fails with an actionable message, and valid bundles pass on Linux runners.

Optimize the GitHub Actions pipeline for the pnpm-based browser extension without weakening correctness. Enable the official pnpm store cache on Node 20 runners, key it from the lockfile and package-manager version, and keep `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` as the source of truth. Apply the cache to lint, test, and build jobs while avoiding shared mutable build outputs. Acceptance: repeat runs show a cache hit, changing the lockfile invalidates it, and all existing checks still execute.

Add a manually triggered rollback workflow for the browser extension's published packages. Let an operator choose a previous Git tag, fetch its immutable GitHub Release artifact, verify the manifest version and SHA, then republish that package to the selected Chrome Web Store or Firefox Add-ons channel using existing secrets. Require an explicit confirmation input, preserve the current release, and write an audit summary. Acceptance: invalid tags and mismatched hashes stop safely, a valid rollback produces a store submission, and no source rebuild occurs.

In our Python/FastAPI service, update Alembic's env.py to make migrations use the DATABASE_URL connection while preserving offline generation. Read the URL from existing settings, avoid opening a second engine, and keep current PostgreSQL schema naming and transaction behavior. Do not alter migration files or application models. Acceptance: `alembic upgrade head` uses the configured URL in online mode, `alembic upgrade head --sql` still emits SQL without connecting, and existing migration tests pass.

In `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, switch the deployment job from the retired `DATABASE_PASSWORD` repository secret to `DATABASE_PASSWORD_V2`, while keeping the username, host, and staging/production environment mapping unchanged. Pass the password only through the existing process environment; do not echo it, write it to artifacts, or change application code. Acceptance: the YAML parses, every database migration and deploy step receives the new secret, no reference to the retired secret remains in the workflow, and the existing PostgreSQL connection format is preserved.

In the Go HTTP service, implement the existing `/health/db-replica` handler in `internal/health/replica.go`. Check PostgreSQL reachability with a context timeout of two seconds, verify that the target is actually a hot standby using `pg_is_in_recovery()`, and report unhealthy when replay lag exceeds 30 seconds. Return the repository's standard JSON health shape and HTTP 503 on failure, without exposing connection details. Acceptance: healthy replicas return 200, failures return 503, timeouts cancel the query, and current handler tests remain green.

In the Rails app, fix `with_advisory_lock` in `lib/database_lock.rb` so a failed migration cannot leave a PostgreSQL advisory lock held on the connection. Acquire with the existing five-second timeout, ensure the lock is released in an `ensure` block even when the yielded migration raises, and preserve the current return value and logging. Do not change migration files or lock names. Acceptance: success and exception paths both release the lock, timeout still raises the existing error, and the focused lock spec passes.

In `infra/README.md`, document the PostgreSQL RDS backup policy already declared by Terraform: seven daily automated backups, one weekly snapshot retained for four weeks, and deletion protection in production only. Include where operators verify or restore backups, identify the staging exception, name the owning platform team, and warn that manual snapshots are not covered by the retention rule. Do not invent new infrastructure or change Terraform. Acceptance: the section matches `infra/rds.tf` and gives an unambiguous restore path for each environment.

Create one PostgreSQL migration for the `orders` table that fills `audited_at` from `updated_at` wherever `audited_at` is currently NULL, leaving existing values untouched. Run it in bounded batches or a single indexed update appropriate for the repository's migration conventions, and make the operation safe to retry. Do not alter the column type, defaults, or application code. Acceptance: applying the migration backfills every eligible row, rerunning it changes zero rows, and the migration's checks pass on the existing test database.

In the Node.js service's `config/database.ts`, harden the existing `pg` pool without changing callers or the connection URL. Set a default maximum of 10 clients, an idle timeout of 30 seconds, and a connection timeout of 5 seconds, with each value overridable by the repository's existing environment-variable convention. Keep SSL handling unchanged and avoid logging credentials. Acceptance: the pool receives numeric values, invalid overrides fall back safely to defaults, and the database configuration tests pass.

In the Django project, update the single database router in `app/db_router.py` to send read-only operations for the `analytics` app to the configured `replica` alias, while all writes, migrations, and unrelated apps continue using `default`. Preserve existing relation and migration decisions. Do not add a new backend or change settings files. Acceptance: `db_for_read` returns `replica` only for analytics reads, `db_for_write` remains `default`, and the router unit tests cover both aliases.

Add one PostgreSQL migration that removes the two obsolete non-unique indexes `idx_events_old_status` and `idx_events_legacy_type` from `events`. Use the migration framework's PostgreSQL-safe concurrent index operation and mark the migration non-transactional if required. Do not drop primary-key, unique, or currently referenced indexes, and provide the repository-standard rollback behavior. Acceptance: the migration applies on PostgreSQL without a transaction error, the named indexes disappear, and rollback restores them.

Add a `db-status` command to the existing Python Click CLI in `cli/database.py`, using the repository's Alembic configuration rather than issuing custom SQL. Print the current revision and whether the database is ahead, behind, or at head; return exit code 0 for up-to-date and 1 for drift or connection failure. Keep output plaintext for CI and avoid printing the connection string. Acceptance: the command works with the existing `DATABASE_URL`, handles an unavailable database cleanly, and the CLI tests pass.

In `config/database.yml` for the Rails application, cap the production PostgreSQL connection pool at 10 while allowing `DB_POOL` to override it using the existing ERB and environment pattern. Leave development, test, adapter, checkout, and timeout settings unchanged. Ensure the value is emitted as an integer and does not silently become an empty string when the variable is absent. Acceptance: production defaults to 10, a valid `DB_POOL=20` yields 20, and the configuration test suite passes.

Implement the existing Prisma seed entry point in `prisma/seed.ts` for local development only. Insert a deterministic organization, one admin user, and two sample projects using stable IDs or unique keys, and make the script idempotent with `upsert` so rerunning it creates no duplicates. Read no production credentials and do not modify the schema or deployment commands. Acceptance: `prisma db seed` succeeds against a fresh PostgreSQL database, can run twice safely, and leaves exactly the documented sample records.

Implement a Vault-backed secret delivery subsystem for Kubernetes workloads across staging and production. Use HashiCorp Vault with Kubernetes auth, the External Secrets Operator, and Terraform-managed policies; support namespace-scoped paths, short-lived database credentials, rotation without pod restarts, and break-glass access with MFA. Integrate with the existing GitHub Actions deployment flow without committing secrets, document onboarding and revocation, and preserve least privilege. Acceptance: sample services consume rotated secrets, policy tests pass, failed authentication is observable, audit events reach the central SIEM, and rollback restores the previous secret safely.

Harden the GitHub Actions deployment pipeline for production infrastructure and services. Replace long-lived cloud keys with GitHub OIDC and short-lived role assumption, isolate build, test, deploy, and approval permissions, pin third-party actions by digest, and add protected environments with required reviews. Generate tamper-evident logs, prevent secrets from appearing in output, and support emergency rollback through a separately authorized workflow. Acceptance: a pull request cannot deploy directly, unauthorized workflow changes fail policy checks, staging and production use distinct roles, audit records identify the actor and commit, and documented recovery steps work in a test repository.

Build automated rotation for AWS IAM and database credentials used by services, CI, and scheduled jobs. Use IAM roles and STS wherever possible, AWS Secrets Manager for unavoidable secrets, and a Lambda or Step Functions workflow for staged rotation with overlap and rollback. Inventory current consumers, update SDK configuration and Kubernetes integrations, alert on failed or overdue rotations, and remove obsolete keys only after health checks succeed. Acceptance: all in-scope credentials have owners and rotation intervals, production rotation completes without downtime, revoked credentials are rejected, failures page the on-call team, and an auditable report proves no static key remains in the repository.

Design and implement zero-trust networking between services running in multiple Kubernetes clusters and cloud accounts. Use Cilium network policy, SPIFFE/SPIRE-issued workload identities, and mTLS for service-to-service traffic; define explicit ingress and egress policy rather than relying on namespace boundaries. Provide a migration mode that observes denied flows before enforcement, integrate identity and policy events with the SIEM, and document exceptions for legacy services. Acceptance: unauthorized cross-namespace and cross-cluster calls are blocked, approved traffic remains healthy during certificate rotation, policies are tested in CI, operators can trace an allowed or denied request, and rollback is controlled and time-limited.

Create an end-to-end secrets detection and remediation program for the repository and delivery process. Add Gitleaks or TruffleHog pre-commit hooks, pull-request scanning, default-branch and full-history scans, artifact scanning, and GitHub push protection integration. Maintain a reviewed encrypted allowlist for unavoidable test fixtures, route confirmed findings to the security queue, automatically revoke exposed credentials where provider APIs support it, and prevent noisy checks from being bypassed. Acceptance: historical findings are triaged, new high-confidence secrets block merges and releases, false positives have an owner and expiry, leaked credentials are rotated, and dashboards show coverage, age, and remediation status.

Implement a security incident response automation layer connecting PagerDuty, Slack, AWS, Kubernetes, and the central SIEM. Define severity-based playbooks for credential exposure, suspicious workload activity, and unauthorized deployment; automate evidence capture, token revocation, workload isolation, and immutable timeline recording while requiring approval for destructive actions. Include deduplication, rate limits, least-privilege service identities, and a dry-run mode. Acceptance: alerts create incidents with correlated context, responders can execute and reverse containment from a controlled interface, every action is attributable, evidence survives account compromise, and tabletop exercises demonstrate documented response times and successful recovery.

Create a reusable Terraform security baseline for AWS accounts and Kubernetes platforms. Cover provider and state hardening, encrypted logging, centralized CloudTrail, IAM guardrails, private networking, restricted security groups, key management, backup defaults, and mandatory resource tags. Encode preventive checks with OPA or Conftest and supplementary static analysis, publish versioned modules, and provide an adoption path for existing environments without breaking workloads unexpectedly. Acceptance: new plans fail on critical violations, exceptions require an owner and expiry, baseline modules are tested across staging and production accounts, drift is reported, state never contains unmanaged credentials, and the runbook explains rollout, remediation, and rollback.

Establish verifiable container supply-chain security from source commit through Kubernetes admission. Update GitHub Actions and BuildKit builds to produce reproducible images, generate SBOMs with Syft, scan with Grype, sign images and attestations with Cosign, and publish provenance to the registry. Add a Kyverno or OPA admission policy that permits only trusted registries, approved signatures, and vulnerability exceptions with expiry. Acceptance: every production image has traceable source and SBOM metadata, critical findings block release unless explicitly approved, unsigned images cannot deploy, verification works during key rotation, and operators can identify affected workloads for a vulnerable dependency.

Design a policy-as-code enforcement system for the Kubernetes fleet using Kyverno or Gatekeeper, with policies stored and reviewed in Git. Enforce pod security, restricted capabilities, image provenance, network exposure, encryption requirements, approved registries, and workload identity; distinguish audit, warn, and deny modes for migration. Add reusable tests, policy bundles per environment, an exception workflow with expiration and ownership, and metrics for violations and bypasses. Acceptance: critical policies deny noncompliant production resources, staging provides actionable feedback, existing workloads have a tracked migration plan, policy changes require review and CI validation, and cluster administrators can prove enforcement through exported audit records.

Centralize and normalize privileged-access auditing across AWS, Kubernetes, GitHub, CI/CD, and the production bastion. Collect CloudTrail, Kubernetes audit logs, GitHub audit events, SSO authentication, and role-assumption records into the existing SIEM with immutable retention and synchronized timestamps. Define correlation fields for user, workload, ticket, source IP, and commit; create detections for privilege escalation, unusual geography, disabled logging, and break-glass use; and expose a review dashboard. Acceptance: security can reconstruct a sample administrative change end to end, alerts reach the on-call channel, retention meets policy, ingestion gaps are visible, and quarterly access reviews produce exportable evidence.

Implement a signed-release system for application binaries, container images, Helm charts, and Terraform modules. Use Sigstore Cosign with keyless or KMS-backed signing, generate SLSA-compatible provenance in GitHub Actions, publish attestations alongside artifacts, and define verification libraries and CLI checks for deployment and consumption. Protect signing permissions with isolated environments and approvals, support key or certificate rotation, and preserve verification during rollback. Acceptance: each production artifact maps to an approved commit and workflow identity, unsigned or tampered artifacts are rejected by release gates, downstream Kubernetes and package consumers verify signatures, provenance is queryable, and a documented emergency recovery path does not permit silent bypasses.

Build a secure disaster-recovery subsystem for the production platform, covering PostgreSQL, object storage, Kubernetes state, Terraform state, and critical secrets. Use encrypted cross-account backups, immutable retention or object lock, least-privilege restore roles, regional replication, and documented recovery ordering. Define RPO and RTO targets, detect backup tampering and failures, and create automated restore validation in an isolated account without exposing customer data. Acceptance: scheduled backups are monitored, a full restore drill meets the agreed RPO/RTO, applications pass post-restore health and security checks, credentials are safely reissued, evidence is retained, and operators can recover from both regional outage and ransomware scenarios.

pair.short: Rename FHIR CI to FHIR Verification
pair.full: In `.github/workflows/fhir-ci.yml`, change the GitHub Actions workflow display name from `FHIR CI` to `FHIR Verification`. Keep triggers, jobs, permissions, and steps unchanged. Acceptance: the YAML remains valid and only that name changes.

In `services/patient-api/Dockerfile`, add exactly one trailing LF after the final instruction. Do not change any Dockerfile content, image, or formatting. Acceptance: the file ends with LF and all existing build instructions remain unchanged.

From the repository root, run `helm template patient-api deploy/chart --namespace clinical`. Do not modify files or contact a cluster. Acceptance: Helm exits 0 and emits rendered Kubernetes YAML without parsing or values errors.

In `deploy/kustomize/overlays/staging/kustomization.yaml`, set `namespace` from `health-staging` to `clinic-staging` for the FHIR staging overlay. Preserve image tags, patches, and resource names. Acceptance: the YAML parses and contains exactly `namespace: clinic-staging`.

pair.short: Plan staging audit bucket with Terraform
pair.full: From the repository root, run `terraform plan -chdir=infra/staging -out=tfplan` for the staging audit-log bucket. Do not apply changes or edit files. Acceptance: Terraform exits 0 and writes `infra/staging/tfplan`.

In `deploy/gateway/deployment.yaml`, change only the healthcare gateway container image from `nginx:1.27` to `nginx:1.27.1`. Preserve replicas, ports, probes, and environment variables. Acceptance: the manifest contains exactly `image: nginx:1.27.1` and remains valid YAML.

pair.short: Document Kafka health check in runbook
pair.full: In `docs/runbook.md`, under the Kafka troubleshooting heading, add this command verbatim: `docker compose exec kafka kafka-broker-api-versions --bootstrap-server localhost:9092`. Leave existing text unchanged. Acceptance: the command appears once in that section.

Run `kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f deploy/secrets/fhir-secret.example.yaml` to validate the example Secret manifest. Do not contact a cluster or modify files. Acceptance: kubectl exits 0 with no YAML or schema errors.

In `deploy/patient-api/service.yaml`, remove only `health.example.com/readiness: legacy` from Service metadata. Keep labels, ports, selectors, and other annotations unchanged. Acceptance: the annotation is absent and the YAML still parses.

From the repository root, run `diff -u infra/staging/.terraform.lock.hcl infra/production/.terraform.lock.hcl`. Do not edit either lockfile. Acceptance: report any provider-version difference, including the healthcare AWS provider, regardless of diff exit status.

Run `kubectl get events -n clinical --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Pod --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -n 20` without changing cluster state. Acceptance: output the 20 newest pod events in `clinical`, or fewer if fewer exist.

From the repository root, run `git reset --soft HEAD~1` to undo the newest local commit while preserving staged changes. Do not delete files or modify working-tree content. Acceptance: HEAD moves back one commit and the changes remain staged.

Fix intermittent FHIR R4 synchronization failures between a TypeScript/Node.js integration service and PostgreSQL clinical storage. Preserve idempotency for Patient, Encounter, Observation, and MedicationRequest resources; handle pagination, conditional updates, transient 429/5xx retries, malformed resources, and out-of-order webhook delivery. Add reconciliation jobs, PHI-redacted audit logging, metrics, and dead-letter replay tooling. Acceptance criteria: replayed bundles create one canonical record, no valid data is lost, retry exhaustion is observable, and integration and contract tests pass against mocked and HAPI FHIR servers.

Fix the multi-step patient intake workflow in the React frontend and Django REST backend. Draft data must survive refreshes and partial network failures, validation must remain consistent between client and server, and duplicate submissions must not create duplicate patients or encounters. Preserve HIPAA-safe logging, file-upload scanning, consent capture, and accessibility behavior. Acceptance criteria: users can resume abandoned forms, retries are idempotent, server-side validation errors map to the correct fields, uploaded documents remain associated with the intake, and end-to-end tests cover failure and recovery paths.

Fix duplicate and misordered laboratory results in the HL7 v2 ingestion pipeline, implemented with Java, Kafka, and PostgreSQL. Normalize message identifiers across sending facilities, safely handle retransmissions and corrected results, preserve specimen and observation relationships, and prevent late messages from overwriting newer verified values. Add replayable quarantine handling, facility-specific parsing tests, monitoring for deduplication rates, and PHI-safe diagnostics. Acceptance criteria: repeated messages are idempotent, corrected results retain history, ordering is deterministic, quarantined messages can be replayed, and regression tests pass for all supported facility formats.

Fix claim-status drift between the Ruby on Rails billing application, payer API adapters, and the PostgreSQL ledger. Reconcile asynchronous payer updates with internal state transitions, including partial payments, denials, reversals, resubmissions, and out-of-order notifications. Define an explicit transition model, make webhook processing idempotent, preserve immutable financial history, and add operational tooling for safe replays and manual review. Acceptance criteria: internal status and balances converge with payer responses, impossible transitions are rejected and alerted, duplicate webhooks have no effect, and end-to-end tests cover representative payer behaviors.

Fix incorrect medication-interaction and allergy alerts in the Python clinical decision-support service. Audit dose-unit conversion, route normalization, active-medication windows, allergy severity mapping, renal-function inputs, and rule-version selection across the API, rules engine, and clinician UI. Results must remain explainable and must never silently suppress a high-severity alert. Add deterministic fixture data, versioned rule evaluation, safe rollout controls, and PHI-redacted diagnostics. Acceptance criteria: known patient scenarios produce approved alert decisions, discontinued drugs are excluded correctly, unit conversions are tested, and latency and regression suites meet existing service limits.

Fix missing and inconsistent audit events across the Go services that handle patient-record reads, writes, exports, and administrative changes. Establish a shared audit contract with actor, tenant, patient, request, timestamp, source, and before/after metadata; guarantee durable ordering despite asynchronous processing; and redact secrets and unnecessary PHI. Backfill only events that can be reconstructed safely, without altering clinical records. Acceptance criteria: every regulated action emits one traceable event, failed writes cannot appear successful, events survive service restarts, retention policies remain intact, and compliance-oriented integration tests pass.

Fix patient-record merge failures in the Kotlin/Spring master-patient-index subsystem. Support deterministic matching, human-approved merges, reversals, concurrent updates, and references from encounters, orders, results, claims, documents, and external FHIR identifiers. Preserve the surviving patient’s longitudinal history, prevent cross-tenant merges, and make every decision auditable. Add transactional locking or equivalent concurrency control, migration-safe reference repair, and an operator dry-run report. Acceptance criteria: merges are atomic, retries are idempotent, reversals restore valid references, ambiguous matches are never auto-merged, and integration tests cover concurrent and partial-failure scenarios.

Fix patient-portal timeouts in the Next.js frontend and GraphQL/Node.js backend under realistic longitudinal-record workloads. Trace slow resolver chains, eliminate avoidable N+1 queries, paginate encounters and documents, move expensive export and notification work to durable jobs, and preserve authorization at every layer. Add bounded caching with tenant-safe invalidation, database indexes, request tracing, and load tests using representative de-identified data. Acceptance criteria: dashboard and chart views meet the existing p95 latency target, large records remain usable, timed-out requests do not duplicate mutations, and no PHI crosses tenant boundaries.

Fix referral-routing errors across the React referral console, Python routing service, and Kafka work queues. Correct specialty, geography, insurance-network, urgency, language, and clinic-capacity matching while preserving clinician overrides and patient communication preferences. Make routing decisions versioned and explainable, prevent duplicate referrals during retries, and recover safely when downstream scheduling or payer systems are unavailable. Acceptance criteria: every referral reaches the correct queue or an explicit manual-review state, reruns are idempotent, urgent referrals cannot be delayed by ordinary backlog, routing reasons are auditable, and contract tests cover all supported payer and clinic combinations.

Fix timezone and daylight-saving errors in the Java scheduling service and Vue clinician calendar. Store appointment instants canonically, retain the intended IANA timezone for locations and participants, and handle recurring visits, DST gaps and overlaps, cross-region users, rescheduling, cancellations, and reminder delivery. Audit API, database, calendar-export, and notification boundaries for accidental local-time conversion. Acceptance criteria: existing appointments do not shift during migration, displayed times agree across supported clients, reminders fire at the intended local time, ambiguous DST input is resolved explicitly, and property-based tests cover timezones and recurrence rules.

Fix crashes and incomplete files in the bulk clinical-data export subsystem built with C#, .NET, Azure Blob Storage, and SQL Server. Support large patient populations through streaming or chunked processing, resumable jobs, cancellation, encrypted temporary artifacts, strict tenant and consent checks, and deterministic CSV, JSON, and FHIR output. Preserve existing export schemas and downstream compatibility while adding progress and failure visibility. Acceptance criteria: exports complete within resource limits, retries resume without duplicate or missing records, partial artifacts are inaccessible, authorization is rechecked at execution time, and golden-file and load tests pass.

Fix care-team authorization leaks in the Ruby on Rails API and React administration console. Model organization, facility, specialty, patient assignment, break-glass access, delegation, and expiration consistently across read, write, search, export, and background-job paths. Invalidate permission caches when memberships or assignments change, preserve least privilege for service accounts, and produce auditable break-glass events without exposing sensitive reasons. Acceptance criteria: unauthorized records are inaccessible through every endpoint and UI route, legitimate cross-facility coverage works, revoked access takes effect promptly, emergency access requires justification, and automated security tests cover tenant, role, and cache-invalidation combinations.

In the iOS SwiftUI repository, calculate 2^10 and append exactly `Math check: 1024` as one new line to `README.md`. Do not alter source code or existing text. Acceptance: that line appears once and `README.md` is the only changed file.

In the SwiftUI iPhone app, edit `Home.swift` so the `tileCount` constant is exactly `12`, the result of 3×4. Keep layout, styling, and surrounding code unchanged. Acceptance: `tileCount == 12`, and `Home.swift` is the only modified file.

In Android Kotlin `Config.kt`, replace the `maxCacheEntries` literal `1024` with the equivalent expression `1 shl 10`. Preserve behavior, formatting, and all other settings. Acceptance: the setting still evaluates to 1024 and only `Config.kt` changes.

In the React Native TypeScript app, update `Rotate.ts` so `sliceAngle` is the evaluated result `60` from 360 ÷ 6. Preserve the existing numeric type and rotation behavior. Acceptance: only `sliceAngle` changes and tests still see 60 degrees.

In the Flutter Dart app's `Gauge.dart`, set the `piLabel` display value to exactly `3.14`, rounding 3.14159 to two decimal places. Preserve the widget tree and locale behavior. Acceptance: the label renders `3.14` and only this file changes.

In Android Kotlin `MathTest.kt`, add one focused assertion that 15% of 200 equals 30 using the existing test framework. Do not refactor or add dependencies. Acceptance: the assertion passes and `MathTest.kt` is the only changed file.

In React Native `Tabs.tsx`, set `tabWidth` to the evaluated value `12`, because 24 ÷ 2 equals 12. Keep its numeric type, styles, and component structure unchanged. Acceptance: `tabWidth` is exactly 12 and no other file changes.

In the SwiftUI calculator view, edit `CalculatorView.swift` so the displayed result for 5² is exactly `25`. Keep the input controls and existing typography unchanged. Acceptance: the result text is `25`, with no modifications outside this file.

In the mobile app's launch test, edit `LaunchMathTest.swift` to assert that `9 + 7` equals `16` using the existing XCTest style. Add no helper methods or dependencies. Acceptance: the new assertion passes and only this test file changes.

pair.short: Label 2×2 grid count as four in Icons.dart
pair.full: In the Flutter app's `Icons.dart`, set the accessibility label for the 2×2 icon grid to exactly `four icons`, reflecting 2×2 = 4. Keep the icon arrangement unchanged. Acceptance: only the label string changes in this file.

Build a multi-tenant deployment platform for university course applications running on AWS EKS. Use Terraform, Helm, Argo CD, and GitHub Actions to provision isolated namespaces, managed databases, secrets, network policies, preview environments, blue/green releases, autoscaling, and audit logs. Support hundreds of institutions without cross-tenant access, with policy-as-code and documented break-glass operations. Acceptance requires reproducible environments, canary rollback, encrypted backups, SLO dashboards, disaster recovery drills, and end-to-end onboarding from repository commit to production.

Create a production observability platform for a distributed LMS used by schools. Instrument Go, Java, and TypeScript services with OpenTelemetry; collect metrics, logs, and traces through Kafka and an HA Prometheus/Grafana/Loki/Tempo stack. Add tenant-aware dashboards, alert routing, exemplars, SLO/error-budget reporting, cost controls, and PII redaction with configurable retention. Acceptance requires correlation from browser request to database query, tested alerts for core learning journeys, multi-region failover, runbooks, and load-tested ingestion at peak exam traffic.

Replace the single-region assessment backend with a multi-region exam delivery platform for high-stakes school testing. Deploy stateless APIs on Kubernetes, replicate encrypted question banks and submissions across regions, use PostgreSQL with logical replication plus object storage, and provide active-active routing, rate limiting, autoscaling, and tamper-evident audit trails. Preserve submission ordering during reconnects and prevent duplicate grading. Acceptance requires defined RPO/RTO, chaos tests, offline resume behavior, accessibility-compatible APIs, security review, and a rehearsed failover that handles the target concurrent candidate load.

Implement a governed education data lakehouse that ingests SIS, LMS, attendance, and assessment events from hundreds of districts. Use Kafka, Debezium, Airflow, Spark, and Iceberg on cloud object storage, with schema registry, replayable raw data, quality checks, lineage, and curated research marts. Enforce tenant isolation, FERPA-aligned minimization, encryption, row-level access, deletion workflows, and pseudonymization. Acceptance requires idempotent backfills, late-event handling, contract tests, reproducible pipelines, cost monitoring, and documented recovery from a regional outage.

Design and operate a conflict-resilient synchronization service for mobile learning apps used in low-connectivity schools. Provide durable bidirectional replication for lessons, progress, submissions, and roster changes using protobuf/gRPC, a versioned event log, Kubernetes workers, and PostgreSQL or FoundationDB for state. Define deterministic merge rules, tombstones, encryption, quotas, and replay tooling without losing student work. Acceptance requires reconnect tests across clock skew and duplicate delivery, bounded storage growth, tenant isolation, observability, schema migration support, and a documented rollout for millions of devices.

Build a distributed, secure autograding platform for programming courses. Accept jobs through a durable queue, schedule isolated Firecracker or gVisor sandboxes, enforce CPU, memory, network, and wall-clock limits, stream results, and persist artifacts in encrypted object storage. Support multiple languages, retries, fair quotas, instructor overrides, and reproducible toolchains. Acceptance requires no sandbox escape in threat testing, deterministic grading for pinned images, backpressure under burst traffic, auditability of every execution, multi-region recovery, and APIs integrated with the existing LMS and gradebook.

Plan and execute a weeks-long migration from the legacy single-tenant school platform to a shared, multi-tenant control plane. Introduce tenant-aware service boundaries, per-tenant encryption keys, schema partitioning, identity mapping, data export/import validation, and dual-write or change-data-capture cutover using PostgreSQL, Kafka, Terraform, and Kubernetes. Preserve URLs, grades, audit history, and integrations while supporting rollback by district. Acceptance requires rehearsal migrations, reconciliation reports, zero cross-tenant leakage, maintenance-window runbooks, customer communication, and measured performance parity.

Build a global content delivery and publishing platform for video, documents, interactive packages, and accessibility metadata. Store immutable source assets in S3-compatible object storage, transcode media with queued workers, publish through a multi-CDN layer, and protect downloads with signed URLs, DRM-ready interfaces, and entitlement checks. Support versioned releases, regional failover, cache invalidation, malware scanning, and legal holds. Acceptance requires resumable uploads, integrity verification, WCAG metadata preservation, tenant isolation, upload-to-publish observability, and tested recovery of a complete course catalog.

Create a research-grade analytics fabric that gives teachers near-real-time intervention signals without exposing unnecessary student identity. Ingest activity events from the LMS, stream through Kafka and Flink, maintain feature tables in a lakehouse, and serve tenant-scoped APIs with Redis and PostgreSQL. Include feature versioning, model-independent pipelines, differential privacy or aggregation thresholds, consent handling, and backfills. Acceptance requires sub-minute freshness for supported events, reproducible historical results, fairness and privacy audits, deletion propagation, SLOs, load tests, and documented ownership for every derived metric.

Build a highly available identity federation service for districts using SAML, OIDC, SCIM, and existing Microsoft or Google directories. Provide tenant-configured mappings, just-in-time provisioning, lifecycle deprovisioning, MFA and step-up hooks, key rotation, session revocation, and audit export. Run the control plane on Kubernetes with PostgreSQL, Redis, and an HSM-backed secrets workflow; isolate tenant configuration and support regional failover. Acceptance requires migration from current login paths, conformance tests with representative IdPs, zero orphaned accounts, rollback, rate-limit protection, and operational runbooks.

Create a distributed job platform for asynchronous education workloads such as plagiarism checks, PDF conversion, rubric scoring, and notification fan-out. Use Kafka or NATS for durable messaging, a workflow engine for retries and dependencies, Kubernetes-based worker pools with per-tenant quotas, and PostgreSQL for job state. Guarantee idempotent handlers, priority classes, dead-letter inspection, cancellation, and artifact retention policies. Acceptance requires recovery after broker and worker loss, fair scheduling under overload, traceable job lineage, at-least-once semantics documented, autoscaling tests, and integration with LMS webhooks.

Implement a multi-region disaster-recovery and continuity platform for the core learning environment. Codify AWS infrastructure with Terraform, replicate PostgreSQL and object storage, centralize encrypted backups, version configuration and secrets, and automate restore, DNS, and traffic failover through Kubernetes and Argo CD. Define service dependencies, RPO/RTO tiers, data-retention rules, and operator approvals for destructive recovery steps. Acceptance requires quarterly full-environment restores, game-day chaos exercises, evidence of grade and submission integrity, monitoring for replication lag, documented runbooks, and a tested return to primary.
